## 10. Scenarios

Each game of Heraldry Skirmish is a distinct **Adventure**, a self-contained battle built from a Climate, a Core Scenario, a Secondary Objective, random weather, and neutral Monsters. Competitive games usually pit two rival parties against one another while both sides race for Coins, objectives, and survival. Solo and cooperative games use the same scenario framework with additional Monsters, hazards, or other pressure in place of an opposing party.

**Defeated Heroes:** In this section, a Hero is **Defeated** while they are **Knocked Out**, dead, or removed from play by a scenario rule. A scenario condition that refers to a party's Heroes being defeated is met when every Hero in that party is Defeated or has escaped the battlefield.

**Party Decisions:** Each party makes one setup roll, generates one party objective, and makes one party choice when a rule calls for one, regardless of how many players control that party. The Party Leader's controller rolls and makes choices for that party after consulting the other controlling players.

**Carried Objectives:** Unless a scenario says otherwise, a carried objective occupies no equipment location. A Hero adjacent to an unattended carried objective may use **Interact [1 AP]** to pick it up. A carrier may use **Interact [1 AP]** to place it in the nearest legal space or give it to an adjacent allied Hero. If the carrier is reduced to **0 HP**, dies, or is removed without extracting, place it in the nearest legal space to the carrier's last position. A Hero carrying it extracts it by leaving through a legal extraction edge or entering a legal extraction zone as the scenario requires. A scenario's own pickup, transfer, drop, or extraction rule overrides these defaults.

**Contesting Objectives:** A combatant who cannot contest or control objectives cannot use **Interact** on an objective or pick one up, and does not count when a scenario checks which combatants control, contest, hold, or occupy an objective, zone, or control point. They may keep carrying an objective they already carry.

**Secondary Objective Extraction:** If a Secondary Objective requires a carried objective or escorted NPC to escape but the Core Scenario provides no legal extraction edge or zone, any battlefield edge is legal for that Secondary Objective only. Before a carrier leaves through this fallback edge, they drop every other carried objective in the nearest legal space. This fallback does not satisfy a Core Scenario, side contract, or other extraction requirement.

**Escorted NPCs:** When an escorting Hero resolves voluntary movement, move the escorted NPC along a legal path by up to the NPC's **Speed**, ending within **2"** of that Hero. The Hero cannot declare movement that would leave no legal final position within **2"** for the NPC. The NPC cannot move through terrain or spaces they could not legally enter.

**Scenario Reward Items:** An item or token explicitly described as a scenario reward is temporary and occupies no equipment location. Unless its rule says it persists or may be used during a future adventure, remove it at the end of the current adventure.

**Scenario-Specific Monster Groups at Setup:** After numbering all Random Monster Groups, assign each scenario-specific Monster Group the next available group number in the order the scenario lists them. Scenario-specific Monsters deployed together under the same heading, starting state, and activation instructions form 1 Group unless the scenario says otherwise.

**Monsters Placed After Setup:** A creature placed after setup by a scenario rule remains a **Monster**, not a **Summon**. A scenario-specific Monster uses their printed profile. One resolution that places one or more Monsters is one reinforcement event. Monsters placed by the same resolution form one Monster Group; when that Group is first formed, assign it the next available group number. Later Monsters placed by the same repeated scenario rule join that Group and retain its number unless the scenario says otherwise. The Group uses the allegiance stated by the scenario, begins **Awake** unless stated otherwise, and uses the placement point or nearest relevant objective as its Guard Point. If placed before the Monster Phase begins, it may activate in that Monster Phase. If placed during or after a Monster Phase, it cannot activate until the next Monster Phase unless the placing rule explicitly says otherwise. A named bestiary Monster placed this way yields **0 CV** and no defeat reward unless the scenario explicitly grants one; a scenario-specific Monster retains their printed CV and rewards. A Random Monster Group generated during setup but deployed later retains its assigned Group, normal CV, and rewards; delayed deployment is not a reinforcement event.

These placement rules apply in every mode of play. No more than **6** Monster Groups may be on the battlefield at the same time. An event that would create a seventh Group fails and places nothing; an event that legally joins an existing Group may still resolve. If a Monster, marker, or objective would be placed in an illegal space, place it in the nearest legal space instead. If no legal space exists within **2"** of the intended arrival point, delay that placement until the end of the next **Monster Phase**. If no legal space exists at that later timing point either, the placement fails.

**Defeated Monster Groups:** A Monster Group is defeated while none of its Monsters remain on the battlefield and none are waiting to deploy or join that Group. If a later reinforcement joins the Group, it ceases to be defeated until this condition is met again.

### Reading a Scenario Before Setup

This subsection is a preparation aid only; it does not add a step to **10.1 Adventure Preparation Sequence** or override any scenario field. Before resolving **10.1**, read the selected Core Scenario from **Primary Objective** through **Tiebreaker** once so setup, scoring, escape, and victory instructions are read in context.

For scenarios that use persistent state, a scenario sheet, tokens, or notes can make that state easier to verify during play. Track only what the selected scenario actually uses, such as the current round or **Pressure Clock**, objective-marker state, Monster Group number and **Awake/Resting** state, Guard Points, delayed entry, or an element waiting to deploy, transform, expire, score, or trigger. The scenario and core rules, not the tracking method, determine the state.

### Scenario Scaling Field Reference

This table explains common scenario fields. It is descriptive unless a field is defined as authoritative elsewhere in this section.

| Field | Use |
| --- | --- |
| **Role Assignment** | Defines competitive roles when a scenario uses asymmetric objectives. Omit this field when both parties use the same objective. |
| **Primary Objective** | Defines what each party is trying to accomplish in competitive play. |
| **Final Random Monster Groups** | Defines how many Random Monster Groups the scenario uses, normally by reference to **10.6.4**. |
| **Awake Groups** | Defines which Monster Groups begin **Awake** and which begin **Resting** at setup. |
| **Minion Swarm** | Defines whether low-LVL Monsters are added through the Minion Swarm rules. |
| **Objective Scaling** | Defines how objective count or objective requirements change with Party Size or APL. |
| **Level Scaling** | Defines how Monster difficulty, objective difficulty, or scenario pressure changes with APL. |
| **Solo/Co-op Objective** | Defines the objective and extraction requirement used when no rival party is present. |
| **Pressure Clock** | Assigns the mandatory solo and cooperative Pressure Clock. |
| **Battlefield and Terrain** | Defines the battlefield size, required terrain, placement restrictions, and special terrain rules. |
| **Objective Placement** | Defines where objective markers, treasure, hazards, or scenario elements are placed. |
| **Boss Deployment** | Defines where and when a Scenario-Specific Monster is placed and their starting state. |
| **Random Monster Setup** | Defines Random Monster Group placement, Guard Points, off-battlefield entry points, and scenario-specific waking rules. |
| **Party Deployment** | Defines where parties deploy and any Setup Roll-off choices. |
| **Special Rules** | Defines scenario-specific procedures and exceptions. |
| **Escape Conditions** | Defines whether and how carried objectives, treasure, or combatants leave the battlefield. |
| **Victory Conditions** | Defines when the scenario ends and how the winner is determined. |
| **Tiebreaker** | Defines the final comparison used when the scenario's normal victory comparison is tied. |

### 10.1 Adventure Preparation Sequence

Use this sequence before every adventure.

#### Setup Roll-off

Whenever a scenario or rule calls for a **Setup Roll-off**, the Party Leader's controller rolls **1d20** once for their party. The higher result wins the roll-off. Reroll any tie. The winning party makes the listed setup choice, such as a deployment edge, Secondary Objective placement, or another procedural decision specified by that rule. If both parties would automatically win the same **Setup Roll-off**, those automatic wins cancel, and the **Setup Roll-off** is made normally. Setup Roll-offs are made before deployment unless a specific rule schedules them later.

In solo and cooperative play, replace the Setup Roll-off with the following procedure unless a scenario explicitly says otherwise: the allied party automatically wins and makes the listed winner's choice. Any choice or roll assigned to the losing party follows **10.5.5**.

**Asymmetric Role Assignment:** A Setup Roll-off winner never chooses between mechanically different scenario roles unless a scenario explicitly states that the choice is an intended reward. When a Core Scenario assigns two different roles, use that scenario's secret-choice or random-assignment procedure.

#### Random Direction

When a rule calls for a random direction, centre an imaginary 8-point compass on the affected combatant, marker, point, or area, then roll **1d8**:

| 1d8 | Direction |
| ---: | --- |
| 1 | North |
| 2 | Northeast |
| 3 | East |
| 4 | Southeast |
| 5 | South |
| 6 | Southwest |
| 7 | West |
| 8 | Northwest |

Before setup, the party that won the **Setup Roll-off** designates one battlefield edge as North. In Grid Mode, diagonal directions follow the diagonal between the corresponding orthogonal directions. Move the required distance in that direction, stopping at the last legal position if terrain, a battlefield edge, or another combatant blocks further movement.

**Battlefield Edges:** The North and South battlefield edges are the **short battlefield edges**, and the East and West battlefield edges are the **long battlefield edges**, even when the battlefield is square. A scenario or rule that names a short or long battlefield edge uses this designation. It does not change the battlefield's dimensions.

#### Preparation Steps

1. **Determine Average Party Level (APL).** Determine each party's APL as described in **Section 6.14**.
2. **Choose Climate.** Select or randomly determine the Climate using **10.1.1 Climate and Core Scenario Selection**.
3. **Choose the Core Scenario.** Select or randomly determine the Core Scenario for that Climate using **10.1.1 Climate and Core Scenario Selection**.
4. **Generate Secondary Objectives.** Roll or choose from the Climate's Secondary Objective table. Record each result; do not place its markers or areas yet.
5. **Generate Weather.** Roll or choose from the Climate's Weather table. Record the result; do not place its markers or areas yet.
6. **Resolve the Setup Roll-off.** Make the **Setup Roll-off** unless the scenario replaces it with another procedure. Record the winning and losing parties for all later setup choices.
7. **Place Terrain.** Determine each party's deployment zone as the scenario describes. If the scenario leaves a choice, the **Setup Roll-off** winner makes it. If the scenario does not describe deployment zones, the winner chooses a battlefield edge or corner, and the other party takes the opposite one. An edge zone extends **6"** from its edge, and a corner zone is **8"×8"**. Place the terrain the scenario requires, then parties alternate placing any remaining major terrain pieces, starting with the party that lost the **Setup Roll-off**. Unless the scenario says otherwise, alternately placed **Impassable Terrain** and **Blocking Terrain** cannot be placed inside a deployment zone. Unless the scenario says otherwise, alternately placed **Blocking Terrain** must be more than **2"** (more than **2** squares in **Grid Mode**) from all other **Blocking Terrain**, measured between the nearest edges.
8. **Place Objectives and Markers.** Set up objectives, Treasure Chests, portals, ritual sites, hazards, and any other special markers required by the scenario, Secondary Objectives, or Weather. If Weather requires multiple markers and does not assign a placer, parties alternate placing them, starting with the party that lost the **Setup Roll-off**. Each marker must be legally placed and outside deployment zones unless the Weather says otherwise.
9. **Generate and Place Monsters.** Determine the required Monster Groups and place them according to the scenario and Monster placement rules.
10. **Assign Guard Points.** Assign each Monster Group's Guard Point as the scenario directs. If it does not, use the default in **9.3**.
11. **Deploy the Parties.** Deploy each party in the zone determined in step 7, following any further scenario instructions. If the scenario sets no placement order, parties alternate placing Heroes, starting with the party that lost the **Setup Roll-off**.
12. **Begin Round 1.** Round 1 begins with the **Initiative Phase**.

*Example, Scenario Generation:* *Two parties begin a campaign skirmish with an APL of 3. They choose the Greenmark Climate, roll a Core Scenario using **10.1.1**, then each party rolls one Greenmark Secondary Objective and one Greenmark Weather result is rolled for the adventure. After terrain and Treasure Chests are placed, they generate four Monster Groups. One group starts beside a wagon, so that wagon becomes its Guard Point. Another group begins near the centre of the map. The nearest landmark to its starting position is a Treasure Chest, so that Chest becomes its Guard Point.*

| 5 | Sun-Drowned | 6 | The Cinder Lord's Obsidian Prison | Reinforce the prison or free the Cinder Lord. |
| 6 | The Mire | 1 | The Reliquary of Edrava Salttide [Intro] | Retrieve and extract Salttide's Reliquary. |
| 6 | The Mire | 2 | The Lizardfolk's Stolen Offerings | Recover the Sunstone Amulet or steal Offering wealth. |
| 6 | The Mire | 3 | The Mire Titan's Fen | Defeat the Mire Titan or extract enough Geodes. |
| 6 | The Mire | 4 | The Blighted Heartwood | Destroy the Heartwood or complete the Syphon. |
| 6 | The Mire | 5 | Salttide's Reckoning | Break the curse or complete the Curse Ritual. |
| 6 | The Mire | 6 | The Serpent's Sunken Hoard | Defeat the Great Swamp Serpent and recover the Sunken Hoard. |

#### Competitive Matched Play Variant

For tighter competitive play, use the following optional setup changes:

- Do not roll on **Weather Tables**. The battle uses no weather effect unless a scenario explicitly says otherwise.
- Use only the **first listed Secondary Objective** for the chosen Climate as one shared objective; do not generate a second Secondary Objective. Both parties may attempt it.
- Apply **10.6 Dynamic Party and Scenario Scaling** normally, including fixed Hero AP, random Monster Groups, and objective scaling. If the parties' **APL** values differ, also apply the **Lower-APL Party Bonus** in **10.6.3**.

#### Secondary Objective Draft Variant

For matched play that keeps random Secondary Objectives while reducing objective luck, use this optional rule in place of the normal Secondary Objective generation in **10.2**. Each party rolls twice on the Secondary Objective table for the adventure's current Climate, rerolling any result already rolled during this step, then keeps one of its two results and discards the other. Both kept Secondary Objectives are open information. Resolve placement and all other Secondary Objective rules normally, starting with the party that won the Setup Roll-off. Do not combine this variant with the fixed Secondary Objective rule in the **Competitive Matched Play Variant**; use one or the other.

### 10.2 Secondary Objectives by Climate

After the Core Scenario is determined, each party generates one Secondary Objective. Solo and cooperative play therefore uses one Secondary Objective; competitive play normally uses two.

**Generating Secondary Objectives.** Each party rolls **1d20** on the Secondary Objective table for the adventure's current Climate. If the second party generates the same Secondary Objective as the first party, the second party rerolls until the results differ. During **Step 8: Place Objectives and Markers**, the parties alternate placing any markers or designating any terrain areas required by their rolled Secondary Objectives, starting with the party that won the Setup Roll-off. These placements cannot directly obstruct the Core Scenario's Primary Objective markers or Hero deployment zones unless the Secondary Objective specifically requires such an interaction.

Two Secondary Objectives are normally active in a competitive adventure; one is active in solo or cooperative play. In competitive play, both parties may attempt to complete or interact with either objective unless the objective's description specifies it is exclusive or competitive.

**Interaction Template.** Secondary Objectives and Core Scenarios use the same template throughout this section. **Setup**, **Trigger**, **Interact [X AP]**, **Success**, **Failure**, **Reward**, and **Special Rules** appear in bold wherever applicable. If an entry omits a field, that field has no effect for that entry.

**Secondary Objective Reward Bands.** Secondary Objective coin rewards use fixed bands. An easy Secondary Objective is worth **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. A routine Secondary Objective is worth **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. A risky Secondary Objective is worth **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. A hard Secondary Objective is worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. A severe Secondary Objective is worth **5 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. An exceptional Secondary Objective is worth **6 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. Use these values for the coin portion of a Secondary Objective reward unless that entry grants a specific non-coin item, token, Power effect, or scenario exception.

**Resolving Interactions.** When a Hero interacts with a scenario element, resolve in this order: confirm the Hero is in the required position, spend the listed AP, make any required **Check**, then resolve **Success** or **Failure** and apply any **Reward** or follow-up effect.

If an interactable element does not list a **Failure** result, a failed **Check** produces no effect beyond the spent AP and any risk already named in that entry. If an element can be carried, dropped, extracted, destroyed, or handed off, its own entry overrides default carry and extraction rules.

**Reward Claims:** Each listed Secondary Objective reward can be claimed only once across all parties. A reward or interaction explicitly permitted per marker, per Hero, per party, per round, or by another recurring procedure uses that printed limit instead. Repeated descriptions of the same reward do not grant it again. Once a reward's applicable limit is reached, it cannot be claimed again; this does not disable other printed uses of that element.

#### Climate 1: Greenmark Secondary Objectives (1d20)

**1. Altar of the Antlered Path.**
**Setup:** Place a 1"×1" **Standing Stone Altar** marker in a secluded, wooded section, at least **8"** from any battlefield edge or Primary Objective. *The stone is marked with three impact dents, slightly warmer than the surrounding rock.*
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make a **SPI Check**.
**Success:** That party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. The Hero receives a **Warding Charm** scenario reward token. Once per adventure, before that Hero rolls one defensive **Check** or one **AD**, they may consume the token to gain **Advantage** on that roll or add **+2** to that **AD** result. The Altar crumbles.
**Failure:** Place **1 Dire Wolf** adjacent to the Hero, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Dire Wolf gains the **Incorporeal** Special Ability for the duration of this adventure. The Dire Wolf is **Awake** and hostile and yields **0 CV**.

**2. Lost Hunter's Secure Cache.**
**Setup:** Place a **Secret Cache** marker (1") at the base of a prominent tree or rock.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check**.
**Success:** That party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and one **Healing Potion**.
**Failure (or looted without first resolving the listed Interact procedure):** Resolve the Snare hazard (**DEX Check** or **1d4 piercing damage**). Contents are still available after the hazard resolves.

**3. Sunpetal Bloom.**
**Setup:** Place one **Sunpetal Flower** marker (1") in an open clearing.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make a **DEX Check** (Careful Picking).
**Success:** The Hero harvests the bloom as a carried objective. If carried by an escaping Hero, it is worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. Once per adventure, the carrying Hero can crush it **[0 AP]** to grant themselves or an **Engaged** ally **+1 AP** immediately.
**Failure:** The delicate flower is crushed and lost. No reward.

**4. Goblin Ambush Signposts.**
**Setup:** The rolling party places three **Signpost** markers (1") along pathways, at least **6"** apart.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to read the Signpost.
**Success:** Reading it neutralizes it. For each deactivated signpost, the party gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** The first time a Hero moves within **2"** of an active Signpost without first reading it successfully, mark that Signpost as triggered and place **1d3 Beastman** within **3"** of it, using the canonical bestiary entry. The placed Monsters are **Awake** and hostile. A triggered Signpost cannot trigger again or be neutralized.

**5. Sacred Deer of the Grove.**
**Setup:** Place a **Majestic Stag** marker (**HP 6 | AV 0 | SPD 8" | Sz M | LVL 2**, Neutral Beast) in a central wooded area. The Stag has no attacks or AP, takes no actions or Reactions, does not activate, and may be targeted normally.
**Reward:** If unharmed and on the battlefield at the end of Round 5, they vanish, leaving a **Fey-Touched Antler** scenario reward token. The party whose Hero is closest to the token claims it. Once during this adventure, the bearer gains **Advantage** on one **SPI Check** made to resist an effect that would apply **Frightened**, **Sleeping**, or **Silenced**, or force their movement, attacks, or target choices, caused by a forest spirit, Fey ancestry rule, or Greenmark scenario effect. If the Stag is secured instead, they are a carried objective worth **5 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** if escaped with.
**Special Rules:** The Stag flees if they take damage, if a Monster moves within **3"**, or if a Check to secure them fails. When the Stag flees, immediately move them up to their **Speed** along the shortest legal path toward the nearest battlefield edge; determine ties randomly. If they reach an edge, or are reduced to **0 HP**, remove them and fail this objective. A Hero adjacent to the Stag may use **Interact [2 AP]** and pass a **SPI Check** to calm and secure the Stag as a carried objective; while secured, the Stag does not flee.

**6. Entangling Bramble Patch.**
**Setup:** Designate a **4"×4"** area as Dense Brambles. The area is **Difficult Terrain**. Place a Lost Satchel marker in the centre.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to the Lost Satchel may make a **DEX Check** to retrieve it.
**Success:** The Hero retrieves the Lost Satchel.
**Failure:** That Hero becomes **Immobilized** until they spend **1 AP** to free themselves. That Hero then suffers **1 piercing damage**.
**Reward:** Retrieving the Lost Satchel grants **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and a **Thorn-Woven Charm** scenario reward token. Once during this adventure, when an enemy makes a melee attack against the carrying Hero, the Hero may consume the token before damage is rolled. The attacker suffers **1d4 piercing damage** after the triggering attack resolves.
**Special Rules:** A Hero moving through the Dense Brambles must make a **DEX Check** for each **1"** moved. On a failure, that Hero becomes **Immobilized** until they spend **1 AP** to free themselves.

**7. Abandoned Hunter's Lean-To.**
**Setup:** Place a **Lean-To** marker (2"×1") against a battlefield edge or large terrain piece.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check**.
**Success:** The Hero finds **1d2** useful items (**1d6**: 1–2 **Bandages**, 3–4 **Snare**, 5 **Healing Potion**, 6 **Oil of Lesser Sharpness**) and **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** Disturbs a Giant Tarantula nest. Place **1d3 Giant Tarantulas** adjacent to the Hero, using the canonical bestiary entry. The placed combatants are **Awake** and hostile.

**8. Sleeping Forest Guardian.**
**Setup:** Place one **Dire Wolf** if **APL** is **1–2**, or one **Dire Bear** if **APL** is **3+**, in a cave or thicket, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Guardian starts **Resting**. Each time a wake trigger from **9.4** other than suffering damage occurs, roll **1d6**: the Guardian becomes **Awake** only on a **6**. The Guardian becomes **Awake** immediately if they are touched, attacked, or damaged.
**Reward:** If the party whose objective this is completes the Core Scenario's Primary Objective without waking the Guardian, that party gains **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** An **Awake** Guardian that becomes **Sleeping** does not return to **Resting**, and the Guardian counts as woken for the Reward. While the Guardian is **Resting**, they are not **Sleeping** and gain no vulnerability from that condition.

**9. Runestone of Shifting Paths.**
**Setup:** Place a **Runestone** marker (1") in the centre of the battlefield.
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make an **INT Check**.
**Success:** That party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. They may immediately choose up to two non-objective terrain pieces (max 3"×3" footprint) and instantly swap their positions on the battlefield. Each piece must fit entirely and be legal in the other's former footprint; if the swap is not legal, choose a different pair or move neither piece.
**Failure:** Disorienting pulse. The interacting Hero and all combatants within **3"** become **Stunned**.

**10. Spider Nest Infestation.**
**Setup:** Designate a ruined building/dense terrain as a "Spider Nest". Place **1d3+1** **Egg Sac** markers within it.
**Reward:** Destroying a sac yields **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. At the adventure's end, the party that destroyed strictly more sacs than every other party gains **1 Antitoxin**, provided it destroyed at least one; ties gain no Antitoxin.
**Special Rules:** An Egg Sac has **HP 1** and **AV 0** and may be targeted by attacks. When a sac is destroyed, roll **1d4**. On a **1–2**, place **1 Giant Tarantula** adjacent to the attacker, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Giant Tarantula is **Awake** and hostile.

**11. Lost Child's Trail.**
**Setup:** Place "Small Footprint 1" and "Small Footprint 2" markers in a line toward a specific battlefield edge.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** (Tracking). Footprint 2 cannot be tracked until Footprint 1 has been tracked successfully.
**Success:** Mark that Footprint as tracked.
**Reward:** Successfully tracking both Footprints in sequence reveals a "Lost Child" NPC (HP 3 | AV 0 | SPD 4" | Sz S | LVL 0; no attacks; **Special Ability: Small**) within **2"** of Footprint 2. A Hero adjacent to the Child uses **Interact [1 AP]** to begin escorting them. The Child moves with the escorting Hero, remaining within **2"** at all times; if the Hero cannot move, the Child does not move. If the escorting Hero is Defeated, the Child stands in place until a Hero begins escorting them again. Escorting the Child off any battlefield edge grants that party **6 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and **1 Luck Point** to the escorting Hero.

**12. Wind-Chime Warning System.**
**Setup:** The rolling party places **1d3** **Wind Chime** markers (1") hanging from trees or ruin features, each at least **4"** apart.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to a Wind Chime may make a **DEX Check** to silence it.
**Success:** The chime is silenced and removed from play.
**Failure:** The chime remains active.
**Reward:** The first time a Wind Chime jingles due to an enemy Hero, the placing party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. In solo or cooperative play, the first jingle caused by a Monster grants this reward instead.
**Special Rules:** If any combatant ends a **Move** within **2"** of a Wind Chime, the chime jingles. The first qualifying jingle grants the listed **Reward**. On the next later jingle from that chime, roll **1d4** once, then mark that chime as spent for this rule. On a **1**, place one Beast or Goblin encounter from the Greenmark Random Monster Table within **1"** of that chime at the start of the next **Monster Phase**. Use an encounter whose total **LVL** is no greater than half **APL**, minimum **1**. If no such encounter is available, place **1 Dire Wolf** instead. A spent chime cannot generate another encounter.

**13. Desperate Poacher's Last Stand.**
**Setup:** Place a Wounded Poacher NPC (HP 4 | AV 0 | SPD 3" | Sz M | LVL 0; no attacks; does not activate; a legal Monster target) **Engaged** with one **Dire Wolf** if **APL** is **1–2**, one **Dire Bear** if **APL** is **3–4**, or one **Gorebeak Bear** if **APL** is **5+**. Use the canonical bestiary entry for the chosen creature.
**Trigger:** The Poacher is saved if the party defeats the creature before the Poacher is defeated.
**Reward:** If the creature is defeated before the Poacher, the party that dealt the killing blow to the creature gains **A Hunter's Guide** scenario reward item or **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**, that party's choice. Once during this adventure, before the bearer makes the Check required by a simple hazard's own **Interact** procedure, they may consume **A Hunter's Guide** to treat that Check as a success.

**14. Fey Circle of Illusions.**
**Setup:** Place a 2" diameter **Mushroom Ring** marker.
**Trigger:** The first Hero to enter the Mushroom Ring must make a **SPI Check**.
**Success:** That Hero gains **Advantage** on **Checks** made to disbelieve illusions until the end of the next round. That party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** The Hero perceives one random allied Hero as an enemy until the end of the round. They must choose that Hero as the target of their next attack this round if able, but that attack rolls its base damage dice with **Disadvantage**. The ring then vanishes.

**15. Alpha Predator's Territory.**
**Setup:** Designate one battlefield quadrant as "Alpha Territory". Place one **Dire Wolf** if **APL** is **1–2**, one **Dire Bear** if **APL** is **3–4**, or one **Gorebeak Bear** if **APL** is **5+** within that quadrant. Use the canonical bestiary entry for the chosen creature. They begin **Awake** and hostile.
**Reward:** Defeating the creature yields a **Predator's Trophy** scenario reward token worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. The party gains an additional **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** if no allied Hero entered the creature's territory before they were defeated.

**16. Ancient Tree of Wisdom.**
**Setup:** Mark one large Tree terrain piece.
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make a **SPI Check**. Max 1 attempt per Hero.
**Success:** The next time during this adventure a Hero in that party would gain their first or second Wound from being reduced to **0 HP**, prevent that Wound but resolve their **Injuries Roll** normally. This cannot prevent **Decapitated** or a third Wound. The party finds **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** Roots attempt to entangle. The Hero makes a **DEX Check**. On a failure, they become **Immobilized**.

**17. Blighted Effigy.**
**Setup:** Place a 1" effigy (HP 10, AV 1) with an **Aura 2"**: a Hero ending their activation in the Aura must pass a **STR Check** or become **Weakened**.
**Reward:** Destroying it ends the Aura and grants **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. Upon destruction, place **1d2 Thornling Sprouts** (HP 1 | AV 0 | SPD 5" | Sz S | LVL 1 | CV 0c; **Attacks:** Claw, **1d4 slashing damage**; **Special Abilities:** **Small**; **Plant**) adjacent to the destroyed effigy. They are **Awake** and hostile.

**18. Nymph's Hidden Pool.**
**Setup:** Place a 1" Pool marker.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Drink. Max 2 Heroes per party total.
**Reward:** The first Hero from each party heals **1d6 HP**. The second Hero from each party gains **1 Luck Point**.

**19. Contested Grove of Offerings.**
**Setup:** Place a 3"×3" grove within **8"** of the battlefield centre. The grove contains **3** **Offering** tokens, worth **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** each.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to an Offering token and not **Engaged** may pick it up as a carried objective.
**Special Rules:** If an attack or harmful Power is resolved against a combatant inside the Grove, at the end of that round one randomly determined uncarried Offering token is desecrated and removed from play. At the adventure's end, if one party carries at least one Offering token and strictly more than every other party, one Hero chosen by that party gains **+1 Luck Point** for that party's next adventure. This may raise that Hero **1 above** their normal maximum for that adventure.

**20. Ritual of the Antlered Lord.**
**Setup:** Place a 2" Ritual Site marked with antler-scratched runes. The rolling party is the **Ritualists**, and the opposing party is the **Disruptors**.
**Interact [2 AP]:** A Ritualist Hero adjacent to the site may make an **INT Check** to advance the ritual by **1** success. The ritual needs **3** net successes.
**Interact [2 AP]:** A Disruptor Hero adjacent to the site may make a **SPI Check** to defile the site and remove **1** ritual success.
**Reward:** If the Ritualists reach 3 net successes by the end of Round 6, they gain **6 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and the **Antlered Boon** campaign reward: at the start of that party's next adventure, that party may place **1 allied Dire Wolf Summon**, using the canonical bestiary entry's HP, AV, Speed, Size, attacks, and Special Abilities. Treat "this Monster" in those imported rules as "this Summon." They have **2 AP**, activate during the **Party Phase**, do not use Monster AI or AI Steps, count against the party-wide Summon cap, and are removed at the end of **Round 2**. If the ritual does not reach 3 net successes by the end of Round 6, the Disruptors gain **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and the **Defiler's Mark** campaign reward: once during that party's next adventure, at the start of one **Monster Phase**, one Monster Group of that party's choice rolls its base damage dice with **Disadvantage** until the end of that phase.
**Special Rules:** Ritualists and Disruptors use separate interactions with the site.

#### Climate 2: Ashlands Secondary Objectives (1d20)

**1. Warm Reliquary.**
**Setup:** Place a 1" **Iron Reliquary** marker in a ruined alcove or crypt corner, at least **6"** from the Primary Objective.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to the Reliquary may attempt to claim it. Make a **SPI Check**.
**Success:** The Hero takes the Reliquary as a carried one-shot consumable. Once per adventure, the Hero may open the Reliquary as **[1 AP]**. One enemy within **2"** suffers **2d8 necrotic damage** and must pass a **SPI Check** or become **Frightened** until the end of their next activation. The Reliquary is then empty.
**Failure:** The Reliquary pushes back. The Hero suffers **1d6 necrotic damage**. The Reliquary may be reattempted on a later activation.
**Reward:** The Reliquary is worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** if sold during the **Town Phase** at **The Arcane Spire** or **The Grand Hall**.
*The Reliquary is warm to the touch. It is always warm. One of Mordain Kest's bindings, never recovered, surfacing again. Heroes who carry it report hearing a voice that does not belong to them.*

**2. Sealed Sarcophagus Chamber.**
**Setup:** Place a "Sealed Door" blocking a 2"×2" alcove against a ruin wall.
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make a **STR Check** to force it.
**Reward:** Contains a Treasure Chest yielding **1 Treasure roll with Disadvantage** and one **Silvered Dagger**.
**Special Rules:** When the door is opened, roll **1d6**. On a **1–2**, place **1d2 Undead Warriors** inside the chamber, using the canonical bestiary entry. The placed combatants are **Awake** and hostile.

**3. Animated Statue Hazard.**
**Setup:** Place an ornate statue (**Impassable Terrain**). Do not place its Guardian yet.
**Reward:** Defeating the Guardian yields their **CV** plus a **Clockwork Heart** worth **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** The first time a Hero ends their activation within **2"** of the statue or uses **Interact** with it, mark the statue as triggered and place **1 Undead Warrior** if **APL** is **1–2**, **1 Stone Sentinel** if **APL** is **3–5**, or **1 Iron Golem** if **APL** is **6+**, adjacent to the statue, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Guardian is **Awake** and hostile. The statue cannot trigger again.

**4. Pressure Plate Alarm.**
**Setup:** The rolling party places **1d3** "Pressure Plates" (1"×1") in open floor spaces.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to an untriggered Pressure Plate may make a **DEX Check** to disable it.
**Reward:** Each disabled Pressure Plate grants that party **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. If one party disables every placed Pressure Plate before any Plate triggers, that party gains an additional **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** The first combatant to move onto a plate triggers a loud alarm. All **Resting** Monster Groups within **10"** immediately become **Awake**. Plates are one-use.

**5. Prophetic Mural Fragment.**
**Setup:** Designate one large flat ruined wall.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check**.
**Success:** The Hero deciphers a prophecy. Once per adventure, that Hero can force an enemy targeting them or an ally within **3"** to choose a different valid target. That party gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.

**6. Rigged Offering Urn.**
**Setup:** Place an **Ornate Urn** marker (1").
**Interact [1 AP], Inspect:** A Hero adjacent to the Urn may make an **INT Check** to identify the danger. On a success, reveal that the Urn is rigged. On a failure, nothing happens.
**Interact [1 AP], Neutralize:** A Hero adjacent to the Urn may make a **DEX Check** to neutralize it before looting.
**Success:** The Urn is neutralized. The Hero may loot it and make **1 Treasure roll**.
**Failure:** The Urn explodes. The interactor suffers **1d6 fire damage**, and each other combatant within **1"** suffers **1d4 fire damage**. The Treasure roll is lost.
**Reward:** A neutralized Urn yields **1 Treasure roll**.

**7. Restless Grave Spirit.**
**Setup:** Designate a **Disturbed Grave** marker.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to search the grave after the spirit is dealt with.
**Success:** Reveal the Memento of Regret.
**Failure:** Nothing is found.
**Reward:** The party gains a Memento of Regret worth **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** When the first Hero moves within **3"** of the Disturbed Grave, place **1 Possessed Corpse** if **APL** is **1–2**, **1 Spectre** if **APL** is **3–5**, or **2 Spectres** if **APL** is **6+**, adjacent to that Hero, using the canonical bestiary entry. The placed combatants are **Awake** and hostile to that party.

**8. Oracle Head's Cryptic Clue.**
**Setup:** Place a "Stone Oracle Head" (1").
**Interact [1 AP]:** Ask the opposing party one yes/no question about the location or status of one Primary Objective marker or one Monster Group. The opposing party must answer truthfully. In solo and cooperative play, instead reveal the identity and full composition of one **Resting** Monster Group chosen by the allied side.
**Reward:** The first interacting party also finds **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.

**9. Scattered Legionnaire's Gear.**
**Setup:** Scatter **1d3+1** **Discarded Equipment** markers.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Examine the object or area.
**Reward:** Roll **1d6**: **1–2** broken gear worth **0c**; **3** **Dagger**; **4** **Spear**; **5** **Round Shield**; **6** **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.

**10. Twin Levers Puzzle.**
**Setup:** Place two "Levers" on opposite sides of a chokepoint (at least **8"** apart).
**Interact [1 AP]:** Pull one lever.
**Reward:** The compartment contains **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and a **Warding Gem** scenario reward item. Once during this adventure, when a Power would damage the bearer, they may consume the gem during mitigation to reduce that Power's damage to them by **1d6**.
**Special Rules:** If both levers are pulled by Heroes from the same party in the same round, a secret compartment appears midway between them.

**11. Vulture's Prize.**
**Setup:** At the start of Round 2, place a "Fallen Adventurer" in an open area.
**Reward:** If Heroes reach the Fallen Adventurer before the Vultures descend, they find **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and one **Healing Potion**. If the Vultures descend first, the **Healing Potion** is gone, and the coins are reduced to **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** If no Hero has reached the Fallen Adventurer by the end of Round 3, the Vultures descend.

**12. The Bell Beneath.**
**Setup:** Place a 1" **Buried Bell** marker in the deepest or most central chamber of the battlefield, at least **8"** from any deployment zone.
**Trigger:** The first time any Hero enters within **3"** of the Bell marker, they must immediately make a **SPI Check**.
**Success:** The Hero hears nothing. They gain **+1 Luck Point** usable only on the next **SPI Check** or Injuries Roll they make this adventure. The Bell marker is removed.
**Failure:** The Hero hears singing from below. They gain the **Heard the Song** condition (**-1 SPI**), as defined in **9.7 The Bestiary (The Voice Beneath the Bells)**. The Bell marker remains. The next Hero to enter within **3"** must also make the **SPI Check**. This continues until one Hero succeeds, at which point the Bell marker is removed.
**Reward:** The party that successfully silences the Bell (has a Hero pass the **SPI Check**) gains **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. If the Bell is never silenced, no reward is granted.
**Special Rules:** If **The Voice Beneath the Bells** is on the battlefield from any source, they immediately become **Awake** when the Bell marker is placed, regardless of their current state or distance. *It is considered impolite to ask a Hero what they heard.*

**13. Rigged Pedestal.**
**Setup:** Place a pedestal with a Gemstone.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make a **DEX Check** to remove the Gemstone without triggering the gas.
**Success:** The Hero removes the Gemstone cleanly; no gas is released.
**Failure:** The Gemstone is retrieved, but the pedestal releases Paralysis Gas in **Aura 2"**. Each Hero in the area must pass a **STR Check** or become **Immobilized**.
**Reward:** The Gemstone is worth **5 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.

**14. Illusory Treasure Pile.**
**Setup:** Place a Large Treasure Pile marker that appears to be **3 Treasure Chests**.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to the Large Treasure Pile may make a **SPI Check** to test the illusion.
**Success:** The illusion is dispelled. Place the real Treasure Chest within **3"** of the Large Treasure Pile.
**Failure:** The Hero becomes **Stunned**, then the illusion vanishes.
**Reward:** The real Treasure Chest yields **2 Treasure rolls**. After dispelling the illusion, the interacting Hero may immediately use **Interact [1 AP]** to loot the revealed Chest if legal. This opportunity then ends; either party may loot it normally.
**Special Rules:** If a Hero uses **Interact [1 AP]** to loot the Large Treasure Pile without first testing the illusion, the illusion vanishes and that Hero resolves the **Failure** result. The pile is then removed from play.

**15. Sand-Covered Map Stone.**
**Setup:** Place a flat 2"×2" stone, mostly buried, within **6"** of the battlefield centre.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Uncover the stone. Track the AP each party spends on this objective. Each party that spends at least **1 AP** uncovering the stone gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Reward:** When the stone is fully uncovered, the party that contributed the most AP chooses one: place a **Secret Exit** marker on any battlefield edge point at least **8"** from every deployment zone (its Heroes may escape or extract through that marker as if it were a legal battlefield edge), or gain **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. If contributions are tied, each tied party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** instead.
**Special Rules:** When a total of **4 AP** has been spent this way, the stone is fully uncovered.

**16. Resonant Crystal Skull.**
**Setup:** Place a crystal skull.
**Reward:** The first party whose Hero successfully casts a Power while within **3"** of the skull gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. If the skull never shrieks during the adventure, that party gains an additional **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** Any Hero casting a Power within **3"** of the skull reduces that Power's **NRG** cost by **1**. Each time a Hero uses the skull, roll **1d6**. On a **1**, the skull shrieks; each Hero within **3"** must pass an **INT Check** or lose **1 AP** during their next activation.

**17. Tomb Guardian's Test.**
**Setup:** Mark a doorway "Sealed by Riddle".
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to pass.
**Success:** The door opens, and that party gains **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and **Advantage** on its next Initiative roll.
**Failure:** Place **1 Undead Warrior** if **APL** is **1–2**, **1 Stone Sentinel** if **APL** is **3–5**, or **1 Iron Golem** if **APL** is **6+**, adjacent to the door, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Guardian is **Awake** and hostile.

**18. Haunted Sarcophagus.**
**Setup:** Place one Sarcophagus.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make a **STR Check** to open.
**Reward:** Contains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** When opened, place one **Possessed Corpse** if **APL** is **1–2**, or one **Spectre** if **APL** is **3+**, using the canonical bestiary entry. Place that combatant adjacent to the opener. They are **Awake** and hostile.

**19. Weathered Obelisk of Omens.**
**Setup:** Place a 3" tall obelisk.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Once per party, a Hero adjacent to the obelisk may make a **SPI Check**.
**Success:** That party gains **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and chooses one: the current Weather effect ends and does not apply for the rest of the adventure; or the party rolls once on this Climate's Weather Table and applies the new result for the rest of the adventure.

**20. Sudden Sand Burial.**
**Setup:** At the start of Round 3, the party that lost the Setup Roll-off chooses one Hero from each party.
**Trigger:** Each chosen Hero must immediately make a **DEX Check**.
**Burial Check, Success:** No effect.
**Burial Check, Failure:** The chosen Hero suffers **1d4 blunt damage** and becomes partially buried. A partially buried Hero is **Immobilized**.
**Interact [2 AP], Escape:** A partially buried Hero may make a **STR Check** to free themselves.
**Escape, Success:** Remove the partial burial and **Immobilized**.
**Escape, Failure:** The Hero remains partially buried.
**Reward:** The first party to free a Hero from the burial with the Escape **Interact** unearths buried valuables and gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.

#### Climate 3: Undermarches Secondary Objectives (1d20)

**1. Unstable Rock Bridge Hazard.**
**Setup:** Designate a 3" wide chasm. Place a 1" wide "Rock Bridge" (HP 15, AV 1).
**Reward:** The party causing the final collapse gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** for demolishing the bridge.
**Special Rules:** If the Rock Bridge takes **5+ damage** from one source, or a Monster Group crosses it, roll **1d6**. On a **1–3**, a **1"** section crumbles.

**2. Luminous Crystal Geode Harvest.**
**Setup:** Place a "Geode" on a cavern wall.
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make a **STR Check** to crack it. After resolving the **Check**, roll **1d4**. On a **1**, choose the nearest **Resting Monster Group** whose total **LVL** is no greater than half **APL**, minimum **1**. That group becomes **Awake**. If no such group exists, place **1 Giant Centipede** if **APL** is **1–2**, or **1 Giant Black Widow** if **APL** is **3+**, within **3"** of the Geode, using the canonical bestiary entry. The placed Monster is **Awake**.
**Success:** The first successful Hero gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and **1d2 Luminous Shards**. The second successful Hero gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and **1 Luminous Shard**. The Geode is then depleted. A **Luminous Shard** may be crushed to create a **Light Source with Aura 2"** until the end of the round, or sold for **1c**. All Luminous Shards gained from the same depleted Geode may instead be sold together as a matched set for **5c**.

**3. Spider Ambush Ledge and Eggs.**
**Setup:** Designate a high ledge (**Climb** to reach). Place **1d2 Egg Sacs**, each with **HP 1** and **AV 0**; they may be targeted by attacks.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to an intact Egg Sac may collect it as a carried objective.
**Reward:** Destroying an Egg Sac yields **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. An intact Egg Sac is worth **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** if extracted.
**Special Rules:** The first time a Hero moves within **2"** of an intact sac, mark that sac as triggered and place **1 Giant Black Widow** if **APL** is **1–2**, or **1d2 Giant Black Widows** if **APL** is **3+**, adjacent to that Hero, using the canonical bestiary entry. The placed Monsters are **Awake** and hostile. Each sac can trigger only once.

**4. Subterranean Spring of Vigour.**
**Setup:** Place a "Bubbling Spring" (1").
**Interact [1 AP]:** Drink. Max 1 drink per Hero, 4 total across both parties.
**Reward:** The Hero heals **1d6 HP** and gains **+1 AP** during their next activation. The party that takes the fourth drink finds a Geode worth **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.

**5. Cavern Fungus Grove (Hazard and Boon).**
**Setup:** Designate a **4"×4"** square area as the "Fungus Grove" (**Difficult Terrain**).
**Trigger:** A Hero that enters the Fungus Grove or ends their activation in it must make a **SPI Check** unless they are already attuned.
**Success:** The Hero becomes attuned. Once during the rest of this adventure, they may add **+1d4** to one **d20** roll. The first party with two attuned Heroes gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** Roll **1d4**: **1** **Poisoned [d4]**; **2** **Sleeping**; **3** **Slowed**; **4** **Weakened**.

**6. Lost Miner's Final Stand.**
**Setup:** Place "Skeletal Remains" in a dead-end.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Examine the object or area.
**Reward:** The Hero finds **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and a Journal. A Hero carrying the Journal may use **Interact [1 AP]** to read it. Reading it reveals an **Unstable Wall** marker, placed by that Hero's party on any Cave Wall section at least **6"** from every battlefield edge. The Unstable Wall has **HP 10** and **AV 1**. When it is destroyed, the destroying party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**, and that wall section becomes a **2"** wide open passage.

**7. Echoing Chasm of Nightmares.**
**Setup:** Designate a large chasm.
**Reward:** The first time one party triggers **3** echoes, place **1 Giant Black Widow** if **APL** is **1–2**, or **1 Vrymk** if **APL** is **3+**, using the canonical bestiary entry. Place it at the nearest legal space on the chasm's edge to the combatant that caused the third echo; resolve tied positions under **9.5 Unassigned Choices**. It is **Awake** and hostile. Defeating them yields their **CV** plus **5 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** An **Explosion**, or an attack, Power, or Special Ability whose rules text explicitly states that it produces a roar, scream, wail, shout, or other loud sound, causes an echo if resolved within **6"** of the chasm. The combatant that produced the sound must pass a **SPI Check** or become **Frightened**.

**8. Kobold Scavenger Warren Exit.**
**Setup:** Place a "Tunnel Exit" (1") on a battlefield edge.
**Reward:** If no Kobold escapes through the Tunnel Exit while carrying loot, the party that defeated the most Kobolds gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**; if that count is tied, each tied party gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** At the start of Round 3, place **1d3+1 Kobolds** within **1"** of the Tunnel Exit, using the canonical bestiary entry. They are **Awake**. Instead of normal AI, each Kobold moves toward the nearest unattended Treasure Chest or dropped carried objective and picks it up by ending their movement in contact with it; on later activations, they move toward the Tunnel Exit and escape when they reach it. A Kobold carrying loot that is defeated drops that loot in the space where they fell. Kobolds attack only while **Engaged**.

**9. Ancient Cave Hazard (Swinging Log).**
**Setup:** Place a "Tension Wire" across a chokepoint.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to the wire may make a **DEX Check** to secure it.
**Success:** The wire is secured and cannot trigger.
**Failure:** The wire triggers.
**Reward:** The party gains **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** if the wire is secured.
**Special Rules:** The first combatant that crosses the wire triggers a swinging log. Each combatant in the **1"×3"** line behind the wire makes a **DEX Check**. On a failure, that combatant suffers **2d6 blunt damage** and falls **Prone**.

**10. Predator's "Treasure" Lure.**
**Setup:** Place a **Coin Pile** on a ledge. Do not place its hidden Monster yet.
**Reward:** The Coins are false. When the hidden Monster is defeated, place a Chest yielding **1 Treasure roll** in their space.
**Special Rules:** The first time a Hero uses **Interact** to take the Coins, remove the false Coin Pile and place **1 Giant Black Widow** if **APL** is **1–2**, **1 Vrymk** if **APL** is **3–4**, or **1 Cryptstrangler** if **APL** is **5+**, adjacent to that Hero, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Monster is **Awake** and hostile. If a Cryptstrangler is placed, the Hero must also pass a **STR Check** or be **Pulled** directly toward them until in contact and become **Immobilized** until they spend **1 AP** and pass a **STR Check** or **DEX Check** to escape.

**11. Sulphur Pool and Geyser.**
**Setup:** Place a 2"×2" Sulphur Pool with a Geyser Vent. A combatant ending their activation in the Pool suffers 1 acid damage.
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make a **STR Check** to cap the vent.
**Success:** Cap the vent.
**Failure:** The vent remains active.
**Reward:** The party that caps the vent gains **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** At the start of each **Monster Phase** while the vent is uncapped, roll **1d6**. On a **1–2**, the Geyser erupts in a **Line 3"** from the vent in a **Random Direction** (**10.1**). Each combatant in the line makes a **DEX Check**. On a failure, that combatant suffers **1d8 fire damage** and is **Pushed 1"** directly away from the line's origin.

**12. Predator's Glowing Lure.**
**Setup:** Place a "Glowing Lure" in a dark pool.
**Reward:** Defeating the Lurker yields their **CV** plus a **Bioluminescent Pearl** worth **5 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** The first time a Hero moves within **1"** of the Glowing Lure or uses **Interact** with it, remove the Lure and place **1 Giant Black Widow** if **APL** is **1–2**, or **1 Vrymk** if **APL** is **3+**, adjacent to that Hero, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Lurker is **Awake** and hostile.

**13. Deep Elf Ritual Remnants.**
**Setup:** Place candles and an "Obsidian Knife" in an alcove.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to examine.
**Success:** That party gains "Knowledge of Shadow Magic" (the next necrotic or **Darkness** Power a Hero in that party casts either deals an additional **1d4 damage of that Power's primary damage type** or lasts until the end of the next round; the caster chooses when casting) and **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** The Hero suffers **Disadvantage** on their next **SPI Check** against an effect that causes **Frightened**.

**14. Unstable Guano Platform.**
**Setup:** Place a 3"×3" platform.
**Reward:** A secret strongbox in the pit yields **1 Treasure roll**.
**Special Rules:** When the platform collapses, combatants on it fall **2"** into soft guano, suffer no damage, and become **Prone**. The platform collapses if two combatants are on it, or if an **Explosion** affects any part of it.

**15. Chasm Echoes of Warning.**
**Setup:** Mark a chasm "Echoing".
**Interact [1 AP]:** Shout one yes/no question about the location or status of one Primary Objective marker or one Monster Group. The opposing party must answer truthfully. In solo and cooperative play, instead reveal the identity and full composition of one **Resting** Monster Group chosen by the allied side.
**Reward:** That party gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** for ingenuity.
**Special Rules:** This objective can be resolved once per adventure.

**16. The Lodestone Anomaly.**
**Setup:** Place a **Lodestone** token in a cavern chamber. It projects an **Aura 4"** magnetic field.
**Special Rules:** At the start of each round, **Pull** every combatant within **4"** of the Lodestone **1"** directly toward it. This forced movement does not trigger **Reflex Attack** and stops if blocked by terrain or another combatant. An AP-using non-Monster combatant in base contact with the Lodestone is **Immobilized** until they spend **1 AP** to wrench free. A Monster in base contact is **Immobilized** until the end of their next activation, then wrenches free automatically.
**Interact [2 AP]:** A Hero in base contact with the Lodestone pries loose its magnetic core, making a **STR Check**.
**Success:** The Hero claims the **Lodestone Core** as a carried objective worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**, and the magnetic field ends.
**Failure:** The core holds fast; the Hero may try again.

**17. Dormant Ember Guardians.**
**Setup:** Place a vaguely humanoid rock formation. Place **1 Troglodyte** if **APL** is **1–2**, **2 Troglodytes** if **APL** is **3–4**, or **1 Vault Ooze** if **APL** is **5+**, within **1"** of the formation, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Guardians begin **Resting** and become **Awake** only as described below.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to the formation may deliberately awaken every Guardian.
**Reward:** Defeating every Guardian yields their normal **CV** plus a **Hearthstone** worth **5 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** Every Guardian immediately becomes **Awake** if an **Explosion** occurs within **6"**, or if an effect within **6"** creates, destroys, collapses, or forcibly moves stone or earth terrain. They treat the combatant that caused the disturbance as their **Primary Target** until that target is no longer legal.

**18. Flooded Section with Hidden Current.**
**Setup:** Designate a **4"** long tunnel section as flooded. The flooded section is **Difficult Terrain**.
**Trigger:** Each Hero that moves through the flooded tunnel must make a **STR Check**.
**Success:** The Hero moves through the current without being displaced. The first party to navigate the tunnel without any failed **Checks** finds a pouch with **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** The Hero is **Pulled 1d4"** by the current toward the nearest hazard, or toward the nearest battlefield edge if no hazard exists.

**19. Geode of Minor Prophecy.**
**Setup:** Place a Geode.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to divine.
**Success:** The Hero gains one **Prophetic Boon** token: once during this adventure, they gain **Advantage** on one **Check** made as part of an **Interact** with a Primary Objective element. The party finds **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. The Geode crumbles.

**20. Rumbling Forewarning of Collapse.**
**Trigger:** At the end of Round 2, each Hero on the battlefield makes a **SPI Check**.
**Special Rules:** The Hero that succeeds by the highest margin over **12** senses the coming collapse; resolve ties between parties with a **Setup Roll-off**, and ties within one party by that party's choice. That Hero chooses a **2"×2"** area at least **3"** from every deployment zone and marks it. At the start of the Round 3 **Monster Phase**, the ceiling above the marked area collapses: each combatant in the area makes a **DEX Check**; on a failure, they suffer **1d10 blunt damage**. If no Hero succeeds on the **SPI Check**, the collapse instead occurs centred on a randomly determined Hero's position.
**Reward:** The sensing Hero's party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.

#### Climate 4: Pale City Secondary Objectives (1d20)

**1. Precarious Icicle Formation.**
**Setup:** Designate one ruined archway, high ledge, or overhanging building eave.
**Trigger:** The first time a combatant passes directly under the formation, or an **Explosion** or an effect that a rule describes as a tremor occurs within **3"**, massive icicles fall in a **1"×3"** line beneath it, dealing **1d10 piercing damage**. Each combatant in that line must make a **DEX Check**.
**Success:** The combatant suffers half that damage and does not become **Slowed**. The fallen icicles create a patch of **Difficult Terrain** (**1"×2"**).
**Failure:** The combatant suffers the full damage and becomes **Slowed**.
**Reward:** When a Hero first suffers damage from the falling icicles, the opposing party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** for springing the trap. In solo or cooperative play, the allied party instead gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** if the falling icicles damage a Monster without damaging an allied Hero.

**2. Frozen Sage's Locked Chest.**
**Setup:** Place a **Frozen Chest** marker visibly encased in a block of ice (HP 10, AV 2, **Vulnerable:** fire, **Immune:** ice).
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make a **DEX Check** with Lockpicks to open it, or make a **STR Check** to force it open.
**Reward:** The chest yields **1 Treasure roll** and one roll on the **Tier 1 Scrolls** (**1d2**: **1** = Arcane, **2** = Divine).

**3. Awakening Frozen Statue.**
**Setup:** Place an ornate frozen statue of a warrior. Place **2 Frozen Skeletons** if **APL** is **1–2**, **1 Ice Elemental** if **APL** is **3–5**, or **1 Gelid Fiend** if **APL** is **6+**, adjacent to the statue, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Guardians begin **Resting** and become **Awake** only as described below.
**Reward:** Defeating every Guardian yields their normal **CV** plus a **Heart of Glacial Ice** worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. A Hero may use the **Heart of Glacial Ice [1 AP]** once during this adventure to extinguish normal fire in **Aura 2"**.
**Special Rules:** Every Guardian immediately becomes **Awake** and treats the nearest Hero as their **Primary Target** if a Hero touches the statue, attempts to loot one pre-designated Treasure Chest within **4"**, or resolves a magical fire effect within **3"**.

**4. Icy Rune Hazard.**
**Setup:** The rolling party places **1d2** **Frost Rune** markers (1" each) on open floor spaces.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to spot the rune before entering its space.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to neutralize a spotted rune.
**Reward:** Neutralizing a rune grants **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** per rune.
**Special Rules:** A Hero may examine a rune before entering its space. The first Hero to move onto an unneutralized rune triggers it. The triggering Hero and all combatants within **1"** suffer **1d6 ice damage**; each affected combatant may make a **DEX Check** to halve that damage. The triggering Hero's **Speed** is halved during their next **Move**.

**5. Decipher Glacial Prophecy.**
**Setup:** Faint etchings are visible on a large, smooth ice wall section.
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to decipher. Requires two successful **INT Checks** total (the successes may come from different activations or different Heroes in the same party).
**Success:** The next time a Hero in that party would suffer ice damage, that damage is negated.
**Reward:** That party finds a **Frozen Scroll Case** containing **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** After each failed **Check**, roll **1d4**. On a **1**, create a patch of **Slippery Terrain** at the interactor's feet.

**6. Ice-Bound Supply Cache.**
**Setup:** Place a heavily iced-over crate as a **2"×2"** marker. The ice has **HP 20**, **AV 1**, and is **Vulnerable:** fire and blunt.
**Trigger:** Heroes may attack the ice normally.
**Success:** When the ice is reduced to **0 HP**, the cache opens.
**Reward:** The cache contains **1d3** uses of **Arctic Rations** and **1 Treasure roll**. A Hero may consume **Arctic Rations [0 AP]** to ignore ice weather damage until the end of the next round.

**7. Lingering Spirit of the Frozen Watch.**
**Setup:** Designate one ruined guard tower or outpost.
**Trigger:** When the first Hero enters the guard tower or outpost, place **1 Ice Wraith** adjacent to that Hero, using the canonical bestiary entry. The Ice Wraith begins **Resting** and non-hostile. Until they become hostile, they do not activate, are not an enemy, and are ignored by other Monsters.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to the Ice Wraith may make a **SPI Check** to pacify the Ice Wraith.
**Success:** The Ice Wraith points to a loose floorboard and fades. The Hero finds **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and a **Frozen Watchman's Horn** scenario reward token. Once per adventure, the bearer may use the token **[1 AP]** to grant allies within **6"** **+1 AV** until the end of the round.
**Failure:** After the **Interact** resolves, the Ice Wraith becomes **Awake** and hostile, then immediately makes one listed attack against the nearest legal target. The Ice Wraith yields normal **CV**, but the treasure is lost.
**Special Rules:** If any combatant attacks the Ice Wraith before they are pacified, then after that attack resolves the Ice Wraith becomes **Awake** and hostile and immediately makes one listed attack against the nearest legal target, if able. They yield normal **CV** once hostile.

**8. Frozen Skeleton Lair Entrance.**
**Setup:** A shimmering, web-like crack in ice (1" marker).
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to search.
**Success:** The Hero gains **Frozen Burial Hoard** worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and one **Masterwork Dagger**. The first attack made with that dagger during this adventure that damages a target deals an additional **1 ice damage**.
**Special Rules:** The first time a Hero moves within **2"** of the crack or Interacts with it, mark the crack as opened and place **1d2 Frozen Skeletons** within **2"** of the crack, using the canonical bestiary entry. They are **Awake** and hostile. The crack cannot trigger again.

**9. Shifting Mirror Maze (Illusory Ice Walls).**
**Setup:** Place three **4"** long wall sections. Two are **Illusory Ice Walls**; the third is solid **Blocking Terrain**.
**Special Rules:** At the end of Round 2 and Round 4, the party with the lower total Coin Value chooses one Illusory Ice Wall whose footprint contains no combatants; if Coin Value is tied, use **Random Determination** among those walls. If none is eligible, skip this change. That wall becomes solid **Blocking Terrain**, and the other solid wall from this objective's setup becomes Illusory. An Illusory Ice Wall is **Open Terrain** and may be entered and moved through. For **LOS**, **Cover**, and Areas of Effect only, treat it as **Blocking Terrain**. A Hero adjacent to a wall may use **Interact [1 AP]** and make an **INT Check** to reveal whether that wall is solid or Illusory. The first party to move a Hero entirely through an Illusory Ice Wall gains **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.

**10. Oracle's Frozen Scrying Shard.**
**Setup:** A clear ice shard (1" marker) jutting from the ground.
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to gaze into it.
**Success:** Ask the opposing party one yes/no question about the location or status of one Primary Objective marker or one Monster Group. The opposing party must answer truthfully. In solo and cooperative play, instead reveal the identity and full composition of one **Resting** Monster Group chosen by the allied side. That party gains **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** The shard cracks, releasing a burst of cold. The interacting Hero suffers **1d4 ice damage**.

**11. Haunted Ice Cave.**
**Setup:** A small "Ice Cave Entrance" (1").
**Interact [1 AP]:** Enter and make a **SPI Check**.
**Success:** The Hero finds **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and a "Warmstone" (the wearer ignores ambient ice damage until the end of the second round after it is claimed).
**Failure:** Place **1 Frost Ghoul** if **APL** is **1–3**, or **1 Ice Wraith** if **APL** is **4+**, adjacent to the Hero and using the canonical bestiary entry. The placed combatant is **Awake** and hostile. The cave can be entered only once.

**12. Thin Ice and the Sunken Relic.**
**Setup:** Designate a **4"×4"** Thin Ice area over a frozen pool. Place a **Sunken Relic** token at its centre, visible through the ice.
**Interact [2 AP]:** A Hero on or adjacent to the Thin Ice chops through and lifts the Sunken Relic clear, making a **STR Check**.
**Success:** The Hero claims the **Sunken Relic** as a carried objective worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** The ice gives way. The Hero suffers **1d6 ice damage**, becomes **Prone**, and the Relic remains in place.
**Special Rules:** The Thin Ice is **Difficult Terrain**. If an Explosion occurs within the Thin Ice area, every combatant standing on it falls through, suffering **1d6 ice damage** and becoming **Prone**.

**13. Territorial Tundra Wolf Pack.**
**Setup:** Place a "Tundra Wolf Den" (1") near a battlefield edge.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to search the den.
**Success:** The Hero gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Reward:** Defeating the Alpha yields **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** plus their CV.
**Special Rules:** The first Hero that moves within **6"** of the den triggers its pack. Place one **Tundra Wolf** if **APL** is **1–2**, or one **Blackfire Hound** if **APL** is **3+**, using the canonical bestiary entry. If **APL** is **5+**, also place **1d2 Tundra Wolves** using the canonical bestiary entry. The placed combatants emerge **Awake** and hostile. The first Monster placed by this rule is the **Alpha**.

**14. Ice-Bound Treasure Chest (Double Locked).**
**Setup:** A prominent Treasure Chest is visibly encased in thick ice (HP 10, AV 2, **Vulnerable:** fire). The chest is also locked.
**Interact [1 AP]:** After the ice is destroyed, make a **DEX Check** with Lockpicks to open the chest.
**Interact [2 AP]:** After the ice is destroyed, make a **STR Check** to force the chest open.
**Reward:** The cache yields **2 Treasure rolls** and a **Frost Brand Shard** scenario reward item. A Hero may attach the shard to one weapon with **Interact [1 AP]**. That weapon deals an additional **1 ice damage** during this adventure.

**15. Lost Explorer's Insulated Tent.**
**Setup:** A **Tent** marker (2"×2" terrain).
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to search the tent.
**Success:** The Hero gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and a "Climber's Kit" (**Advantage** on **STR Checks** to **Climb** for one Hero this adventure).
**Special Rules:** Heroes may enter the tent. Heroes inside the tent are **Immune** to negative weather effects in this scenario, including ice damage and **LOS** reduction. Only one party may search the tent successfully.

**16. Crumbling Ice Archway.**
**Setup:** Place a large ice archway as a **3"×3"** terrain feature spanning a key path. The archway has **HP 20** and **AV 1**.
**Trigger:** The archway may be destroyed by attacks or scenario effects.
**Success:** When the archway is reduced to **0 HP**, it collapses.
**Reward:** The party that caused the final collapse finds **Frozen Relics** worth **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** in the debris.
**Special Rules:** When the archway collapses, replace it with a **3"×2" Difficult Terrain** area.

**17. Glyph of Absolute Zero.**
**Setup:** A barely visible glyph (1" marker) in a chokepoint.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** before entering to spot the glyph.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero of the **Caster** or **Hybrid** archetype may make an **INT Check** to neutralize a spotted glyph.
**Reward:** Neutralizing the glyph grants **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Special Rules:** The first combatant to move onto it triggers an **Aura 3"** burst of extreme cold. Combatants in the area make a **DEX Check**. On a failure, each affected combatant suffers **2d6 ice damage** and becomes **Immobilized**. The glyph fades.

**18. Aurora Shard Cascade.**
**Setup:** None.
**Trigger:** At the start of Round 4, place **1d3** Aurora Shard markers randomly within **10"** of the centre.
**Interact [1 AP]:** The first Hero adjacent to an Aurora Shard may claim it.
**Reward:** A Hero may crush a claimed Aurora Shard **[0 AP]**, even while **Stunned**, to regain **1d4 HP** and remove one **Frightened** or **Stunned** condition from themselves. Each unused Aurora Shard is worth **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** at the end of the adventure.

**19. Frozen Sage's Hidden Study.**
**Setup:** A ruined building has a **Secret Door** marker. A Hero outside and adjacent to it may use **Interact [1 AP]** and make an **INT Check** to spot it. Once spotted, an adjacent Hero may use **Interact [1 AP]** and make a **STR Check** to force it open.
**Interact [2 AP]:** A Hero inside the opened study may make an **INT Check** to search it.
**Success:** The Hero gains one **Scroll of Ice Ray** and **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. In addition, that party's next damage roll against the Core Scenario's scenario-specific Monster is made with **Advantage**.

**20. The Aurora Lens.**
**Setup:** Place an **Aurora Lens** token at the battlefield centre and two **Focus Pedestal** tokens on opposite sides of it, each within **9"** of the Lens.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to a Focus Pedestal rotates it to catch the polar light. Each Focus Pedestal can be aligned once.
**Special Rules:** When both Focus Pedestals have been aligned, the Aurora Lens ignites with refracted light.
**Reward:** When the Lens ignites, the party that performed more of the two alignments gains **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**; if each party aligned one Pedestal, the party that aligned the second one gains the reward. The blaze of light scatters the gloom: the current Weather effect ends and does not apply for the rest of the adventure.

#### Climate 5: Sun-Drowned Secondary Objectives (1d20)

**1. Sudden Sand Geyser Eruption.**
**Setup:** At the start of Round 2, place a "Geyser Vent" (1") in an open area.
**Interact [1 AP]:** After the vent erupts, a Hero adjacent to the vent may make a **DEX Check** to gather glassy mineral fragments.
**Reward:** Success grants **2 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. This reward can be claimed once.
**Special Rules:** At the start of each **Monster Phase**, the vent erupts. Each combatant within **2"** of the vent must pass a **DEX Check** or be **Pushed 1d3"** directly away from the vent and become **Blinded**. After the first eruption, the vent's **Aura 2"** area is **Difficult Terrain** for the rest of the adventure.

**2. Shimmering Oasis (Contested).**
**Setup:** Place an Oasis marker as a **2"×2"** water feature near the centre.
**Interact [1 AP]:** A Hero adjacent to the Oasis may drink from it, restoring **1d4 + 1 HP**. The Oasis provides **4** total Drinks across both parties.
**Reward:** The party that takes the fourth Drink finds **Desert Pearls** worth **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. The Oasis then runs dry.
**Special Rules:** Each Hero may resolve this objective once.

**3. Giant Scorpion's Guarded Nest.**
**Setup:** Place a **Nest** (**1"**) and one **Giant Scorpion** starting **Awake** within **1"**.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to search.
**Success:** The Hero gains **Scorpion Eggs** worth **4 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and **Scorpion Venom**. A Hero may apply **Scorpion Venom** to one weapon with **Interact [1 AP]**. The next attack with that weapon that damages a target causes **Poisoned [d4]**. The target must pass a **STR Check**. On a failure, the target loses **1 AP** on their next activation; a Monster uses the normal substitute for lost AP in **9.1**.
**Reward:** The Giant Scorpion also yields their **CV** when defeated.
**Special Rules:** A Hero cannot search the Nest until the Giant Scorpion is defeated or lured away.

**4. Ancient Tomb Entrance Hazard.**
**Setup:** Place "Pressure Plate" (1") inside a Tomb Entrance archway.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make an **INT Check** to spot the hazard.
**Interact [1 AP]:** Make a **DEX Check** to neutralize a spotted hazard.
**Reward:** Neutralizing the hazard grants **3 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and a **Silvered Dagger**.
**Special Rules:** The first combatant to move onto the Pressure Plate triggers the scything blade: they must pass a **DEX Check** or suffer **1d10 piercing damage**.

**5. Sunstone Monolith's Blessing/Curse.**
**Setup:** A Sunstone Monolith (1"×1" pillar).
**Interact [1 AP]:** Touch and **SPI Check**.
**Success:** One weapon carried by that Hero becomes **Sun-Blessed** until the end of the next round and deals an additional **1 fire damage**. That party gains **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
**Failure:** The Hero is drained and loses **1 AP** at the start of their next activation.
**Critical Failure (natural 1):** The Hero suffers **1d6 fire damage**.
**Special Rules:** Each Hero may attempt this objective once. A maximum of **3** total Heroes may attempt it.

**6. Lost Caravan's Secure Strongbox.**
**Setup:** Place a "Wrecked Caravan" (2"×2", **Cover Terrain** tagged **Difficult Terrain**) with a "Locked Strongbox".
**Interact [2 AP]:** Make a **DEX Check** with Lockpicks to open the Strongbox.
**Interact [3 AP]:** Make a **STR Check** to force the Strongbox open.
**Reward:** The caravan contains **Ancient Trade Bars** worth **6 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins** and a **Desert Veil** scenario reward item. Once during this adventure, the bearer may ignore **Blinded**, or may treat their **Hide distance** as **0"** while in sand.

**7. Curse of the Desiccated King.**
**Setup:** Designate one Core Scenario Treasure Chest as the **Cursed Chest**.
**Reward:** If that Hero survives the adventure, their party gains an additional **5 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**. The curse is removed after the adventure ends.
**Special Rules:** The first Hero to loot the **Cursed Chest** gains its contents and becomes **Cursed**.

**8. Constrictor Ambush.**
**Setup:** Place three Ambush markers in separate 3"×3" open sand areas. Secretly and randomly determine which of the three markers is the true ambush marker before play. Do not reveal it until it is triggered.
**Reward:** Defeating every Ambusher yields their normal **CV** plus **1 Antitoxin** and **1 × (2 + (4 × APL)) Coins**.
