#### 11.2.4 Phase 4: Town Phase

During each Town Phase, each party receives **4 Town Action Points (TAP)**.

The party may spend TAP on Town actions available to it. Unspent TAP are lost at the end of the Town Phase unless a rule says otherwise.

Unless a rule says otherwise:

- each listed Town action costs the TAP shown beside it,
- you may visit the same location multiple times,
- and each action is resolved when chosen.

**Town Phase checklist**

1. Confirm current **Storage**, **Treasury**, roster status, and any lingering injuries.
2. Resolve effects that occur at the start of the Town Phase, then gain **4 TAP** or the modified amount specified by a Journey result.
3. Spend **TAP** on legal Town actions in any order.
4. Pay all required coin costs as each Town action resolves.
5. Update Hero sheets, known Powers, equipped items, pending commissions, **Storage**, and **Stronghold** progress.
6. Confirm the party's legal Roster and Active Party before the next adventure.

##### The Grand Hall

The Grand Hall handles trade, brokerage, commissions, and fencing.

- **Buy and Sell Goods [0 TAP]:** Buy **Tier 1** and **Tier 2** items at list price. This normally includes mundane weapons, armour, shields, adventuring gear, **Tier 1–2 consumables**, and non-special enhanced items below **Rare** rarity. Sell unwanted gear for **50%** of base value. If your **Roster** includes at least **1 Merchant**, once during this Town Phase, either resolve one sale at **75%** of base value or buy one item for **90%** of its listed price, rounded up to the nearest **1c**. Multiple Merchants do not increase this benefit. It does not stack with another purchase or sale modifier unless a Town action says otherwise.
- **Commission Rare Item [1 TAP]:** Reserve one specific **Tier 1–3 permanent special item**, one specific **Tier 3 consumable**, or one item with **Enchanted +3**. It is guaranteed to be available for purchase during your next Town Phase at its normal price. You may instead reserve one specific **Tier 4 consumable**, **Tier 4 permanent special item**, or one item with **Enchanted +4** only if the party's current **APL** is **7+**; that item's purchase price increases by **25%**. A party may have only **one** pending commission and may complete no more than **one** commissioned purchase during the same Town Phase. **Tier 5** items, **Legendary Artifacts**, and items with **Enchanted +5** cannot be commissioned or purchased unless a rule explicitly says otherwise. If the commissioned item is not purchased during the next Town Phase, the commission expires.
- **Appraise and Fence [1 TAP]:** Sell up to **two items** for **70%** of their base value instead of the normal sale rate.
- **Recruit Hero [1 TAP]:** If the Roster contains fewer than **8 Heroes** and the party has not added a recruit during this Town Phase, pay **10c** and add one new recruit under **11.1.6**.

##### The Chapel

The Chapel restores the injured, removes afflictions, and petitions for miracles.

- **Chirurgeon's Care [1 TAP]:** Remove **1 Wound** from one Hero. Cost: **6c × that Hero's Level**.
- **Cleanse Affliction [1 TAP]:** Remove one lingering injury (**5.8**) or other permanent negative effect caused by the Injuries Table or a similar injury rule. Cost: **3c**.
- **Quiet the Bells [1 TAP]:** Remove **Heard the Song** from one Hero. Cost: **0c**.
- **Resurrection [2 TAP]:** Choose one Hero with a retained death record and return that Hero to life. Cost: **8c × that Hero's Level**. The Hero returns to the **Roster** with **1 Wound**, regardless of how many Wounds they had when they died. This action cannot return a Hero if doing so would exceed the current roster maximum. Each Hero may be resurrected at most **once per campaign**.

##### The Arcane Spire

The Arcane Spire researches Powers and copies scrolls.

- **Scribe Scroll [1 TAP]:** One eligible Hero creates one scroll of a Tier 1 or Tier 2 **Arcane Spell** or **Divine Prayer** they know. Cost: **60%** of that scroll's standard purchase price. A scroll created with **Scribe Scroll** cannot be sold.
- **Research Power [1 TAP]:** One Hero learns one new eligible Tier 1–3 Power of a tradition they already use. Cost: **6c × the new Power's Tier × the new Power's Tier**.
- **Transcribe Lore [1 TAP]:** One Hero replaces one known Tier 1–3 Power with another eligible Power of the same tradition and Tier or lower. Cost: **3c × the new Power's Tier × the new Power's Tier**.

A Hero cannot learn a Power above the highest Tier they can normally access. A Hero may be the subject of **Research Power** or **Transcribe Lore** no more than **once per Town Phase**.

##### The Training Grounds

The Training Grounds retrain veterans and sharpen technique.

- **Train [1 TAP]:** Train one Hero in the Roster under **6.16 Hero Advancement**.
- **Retrain [1 TAP]:** One Hero may replace one previously chosen **Class Talent** or **General Talent** with another eligible option from the same tier or list, subject to that Hero's archetype restrictions. Automatic Archetype Abilities cannot be retrained. Cost: **4c × that Hero's Level**.

##### The Ironworks

The Ironworks improves gear and reforges prized equipment.

- **Masterwork Upgrade [1 TAP]:** Upgrade up to **2** mundane weapons, Chest armour pieces, or shields that do not already have an Item Quality and have a listed Masterwork value in **7.11**. Each upgraded item gains the **Masterwork** quality. Cost: pay the difference between the item's base value and its Masterwork value, minimum **1c**, per item upgraded. When sold, an item upgraded this way uses its value before the upgrade.

##### The Guild of Keys

The Guild of Keys manages contracts, maps, logistics, and black-market routes.

- **Accept Contract [1 TAP]:** Take one side contract for the next adventure. A party may have no more than **1** active side contract at a time. After the next adventure is generated but before deployment, roll **1d6** to determine the contract term:
  - **1–2 Monster Writ:** Defeat at least **1** Monster Group and have at least **1** Hero extract.
  - **3–4 Salvage Writ:** Extract at least **1** treasure, relic, clue, captive, or carried scenario object beyond any object required for the primary objective.
  - **5–6 Survey Writ:** During the adventure, a Hero must use **Interact [1 AP]** while adjacent to a terrain feature or objective marker within **6"** of the battlefield centre and not **Engaged**.

  If the Core Scenario gives no legal Hero extraction route, a living Hero standing on any battlefield edge when the adventure ends satisfies only the contract's Hero-extraction requirement; that Hero does not leave the battlefield and is not extracted for any other rule. After applying this exception, reroll a term whose required target, object, action, or extraction cannot legally occur in the generated adventure. If no legal term exists after checking all 3 terms, cancel the contract and refund its **1 TAP** at the start of the next Town Phase.

  If the party completes the contract and at least **1** Hero extracts, gain **5c × APL** during Aftermath, using the party's APL at the start of that adventure. If the party does not complete the contract, gain nothing. A side contract never changes the scenario's victory conditions, never counts as a Secondary Objective, and cannot be accepted for the **Triumph Finale**.
- **Map Room [1 TAP]:** Study the next battlefield's known approaches. In competitive play, your party automatically wins the Setup Roll-off in the next adventure. In solo or cooperative play, after generating the next adventure's Core Scenario, roll one additional Core Scenario from the same Climate and choose which of the two scenarios to play. If the next adventure is fixed by a scenario, campaign rule, or Triumph Objective, you instead gain **Advantage** on the first **Setup Roll-off**, search, or scenario **Interact Check** made by your party during that adventure.

#### 11.2.5 Hirelings

During the **Town Phase**, your party may recruit persistent **Hirelings** into its **Stronghold** roster. A Hireling remains on that roster until they are slain, dismissed during a **Town Phase**, or removed by a specific rule.

Hirelings are purchased with **Treasury** funds during the **Town Phase**. Recruiting a Hireling costs **1 TAP** and their listed coin cost.

Hirelings require no recurring upkeep once recruited. A party's **Stronghold** roster may contain no more than **8 Hirelings** total, including Animal Companions. A Hireling may be dismissed for no TAP cost during the Town Phase; a dismissed Hireling is removed permanently and grants no refund.

##### Active Hirelings and Summon Limits

At the start of each adventure, after choosing the Heroes who will take part in that adventure, choose which Hirelings from your **Stronghold** roster will deploy with that party.

The maximum number of active Hirelings for that adventure is determined by the number of Heroes in that party at the start of the adventure.

| Heroes in the Party | Maximum Active Hirelings | Per-Hero Control Limit |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **4**               | **4**                    | **1** per Hero         |
| **3**               | **3**                    | **1** per Hero         |
| **2**               | **4**                    | **2** per Hero         |
| **1**               | **3**                    | **3** for that Hero    |

These limits are checked only when the adventure begins. They do not recalculate later in that adventure if one or more Heroes are removed from play.

When you choose active Hirelings for an adventure, assign each active Hireling to a specific Hero in that party. That assignment is locked for the duration of the adventure.

A Hireling may only be assigned to a Hero whose printed **SPI** is equal to or greater than that Hireling's listed **Min SPI** value.

Use the Hero's printed **SPI** on their Hero sheet. Temporary in-adventure modifiers do not change which Hirelings that Hero may control.

Hirelings, including Animal Companions, do not count against the party-wide limit of **2** active allied Summons. See **2.5.1 Summon Limits**.

##### Specialist Hireling Rules

Unless a profile says otherwise, all Specialist Hirelings follow **6.15 Hirelings** and these campaign rules:

- A Hireling reduced to **0 HP** is slain, removed from play, and crossed off the **Stronghold** roster.
- A Hireling cannot be equipped from **Storage** unless a specific rule explicitly allows them.
- A Hireling never counts as a Hero for Party Size, **APL**, Boss Scale, enemy or scenario scaling, reinforcement limits, objective scaling, campaign progression, or victory conditions. A specific profile or scenario may still let a Hireling carry or interact with an objective without changing any of those values.

#### 11.2.6 Animal Companions

An **Animal Companion** is a subtype of **Hireling** representing a trained beast, bonded combatant, or other persistent animal ally.

Animal Companions are recruited, rostered, assigned, and limited exactly like any other **Hireling** unless a more specific rule says otherwise. They count against the party's active **Hireling** cap and against their controller's personal **Hireling** limit.

Animal Companions are harder to command than most mortal retainers. For that reason, their **Min SPI** values are often higher than those of similarly priced humanoid **Hirelings**.

All Animal Companions have the **Beast** tag.

Animal Companions use the following additional rules:

- An Animal Companion has **2 AP** each round unless their profile says otherwise.
- An Animal Companion activates during the **Party Phase** like any other allied combatant.
- An Animal Companion cannot use normal equipment unless a rule explicitly says otherwise.
- An Animal Companion cannot open doors, pull levers, carry treasure, take **Interact** actions, or carry, claim, or score scenario markers unless their profile explicitly allows it.
- An Animal Companion does not gain Levels.
- An Animal Companion reduced to **0 HP** is slain, removed from play, and crossed off the **Stronghold** roster.
- An Animal Companion is affected by any rule that targets a combatant with the **Beast** tag.
- Unless a rule says otherwise, an Animal Companion has **0 CV** when removed from play.

If a class feature, item, or campaign reward grants an Animal Companion, add that model to the party's **Stronghold** roster unless that rule says otherwise.

##### Animal Companion Roster

All Animal Companions in this roster have **0 CV**. The listed **Cost** is the amount paid to recruit that companion during the **Town Phase**.

| Animal Companion | Min SPI | Cost | SPD | Sz | HP | AV | Attack | Special Abilities |

This permission does not allow them to control or score any other objective. **Sure-Footed:** Ignore **Difficult Terrain** while carrying an objective. Cannot take the **Hide** action. |

##### Companion Control and Replacement

An Animal Companion always has a controlling **Hero**, as any other **Hireling** does.

If a controlling **Hero** dies, retires, is removed from play, or otherwise ceases to be a legal controller, reassign that Animal Companion to another allied **Hero** immediately after the current action or effect resolves if doing so is legal. If no legal controller is available, remove that Animal Companion from the battlefield. An Animal Companion removed only for lacking a legal controller remains on the Stronghold roster if they were not slain.

If an Animal Companion is slain, they are lost permanently unless a specific rule says otherwise. You may recruit a replacement normally during a later **Town Phase**.

### 11.3 Building the Stronghold

A competitive campaign uses the **Stronghold** race in **11.1.1 Campaign Goal**. A **Stronghold** has **10** available **Components**. The cost of a Component depends on how many Components your party has already completed, not on which Component you choose.

| Components already completed | Cost of the next Component |
| ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 130c |
| 1 | 170c |
| 2 | 210c |
| 3 | 250c |
| 4 | 290c |
| 5 or more | 290c |

Completing 5 different Components therefore costs **1050c** in total. In a campaign that continues past **Triumph**, each further Component costs **290c**.

You may purchase any **Component** during the **Town Phase** if you have the coins to do so. Purchasing a **Component** costs **1 TAP**, and you may purchase no more than **1 Component** during the same **Town Phase**.

If one party purchases its **fifth different** Stronghold Component during a Town Phase, finish both parties' current Town Phase. That party then achieves **Triumph** and the campaign ends. If both parties purchase their fifth different Component during the same Town Phase, both achieve **Triumph** and the campaign ends in a shared victory.

If the campaign continues after **Triumph**, a party may continue improving its **Stronghold**. Each completed **Component** grants 1 permanent campaign benefit.

A **Vault Reserve** is temporary spending power. It can be spent only during the **Town Phase** in which it is gained. It is not added to the **Treasury**, cannot be saved, and cannot be used for costs outside its listed categories. An item purchased using a **Vault Reserve** cannot be sold.

#### The Vault

*The Vault is not a treasury. It is a sealed confession of greed, iron-bound and watched by clerks who sleep in shifts. They count each coin as if the dead might come back to collect.*

*Parties build the Vault below ground, behind murder-holes, false doors, and oath-locked chests. In the Dying Lands, wealth is not owned until it has survived the night.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** During each **Town Phase**, gain a **Vault Reserve** of **20c**. During that **Town Phase**, you may spend this reserve on equipment, items, Hirelings, and services. It cannot pay Training Costs, Retirement Payouts, or **Stronghold Components**. Unspent reserve is lost at the end of the **Town Phase**.

#### The Barracks

*The Barracks smell of straw, old sweat, damp wool, and boiled leather. Names are carved into the beams by people who expected to return. Few are still spoken.*

*A completed Barracks gives a party bodies, discipline, and replacements before grief has finished its work. The Bastions call this resilience. Adventurers call it another chance to bleed.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** Once during each **Town Phase**, when a Hero uses **Train [1 TAP]**, reduce that Training Cost by **10c**.

#### The Armoury

*The Armoury smells of oil, wet leather, coal smoke, and old violence. Its walls hold blades recovered from drowned shrines, shields hammered flat after dragon-fire, and helms whose former owners are better left unnamed.*

*A party with an Armoury does not look safe. It looks prepared. In the Dying Lands, that is close enough to hope.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** At the start of each adventure, choose 1 Hero in your Active Party. Choose one equipped mundane weapon or **Chest** armour; it gains **Enchanted +1** until the end of that adventure. Alternatively, choose one equipped mundane shield; it gains **Masterwork** until the end of that adventure.

#### The Apothecary

*The Apothecary is built around heat, glass, knives, bone saws, and the bitter stink of herbs that should not grow in clean soil. Its shelves hold tinctures from The Mire, salts from the Sun-Drowned, and poultices learned from surgeons paid in secrets.*

*No one leaves untouched. The fortunate leave with scars closed. The unlucky leave with something inside them quieted rather than cured.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** Once per adventure, when a Hero in your Active Party would gain a Wound, ignore that Wound.

#### The Outer Walls

*The Outer Walls declare that the dark must work harder. Stone, timber, ditch, spike, and warding nail stand between the party's claim and the things that circle after sundown.*

*No wall in the Dying Lands is permanent. A completed wall only means the first wave breaks against something other than the door.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** When your party rolls on a **Journey Table**, roll twice and choose either result.

#### The Arcanum

*The Arcanum rises too thin and too tall. Its upper windows burn at hours when honest fires should be dead. Brass instruments turn toward storms, old constellations, and places where the sky has not healed.*

*Every Bastion mistrusts an Arcanum. Every party that owns one learns why, then keeps using it anyway.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** Once per adventure, after a Hero in your Active Party fails a **Casting Check**, they may reroll that Check. They must use the new result.

#### The Stronghold Chapel

*The Chapel is small, cold, and crowded with votive offerings from those who survived by inches. Its saints are chipped. Its relics are suspect. Its candles burn low even when no wind enters.*

*The Chapel does not promise salvation. It gives the desperate a place to kneel before they return to the roads that nearly killed them.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** Once during each **Town Phase**, one Hero may take **Chirurgeon's Care [1 TAP]** without paying its Coin cost.

#### The War Room

*The War Room is where contracts are signed, debts are denied, and maps are stained. Its hearth burns beneath banners taken from ruins, enemies, and dead patrons.*

*A party with a War Room becomes visible. Petitioners arrive. Rivals take note. Every whispered bargain begins to sound like law.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** Your party gains **+2** on Initiative rolls.

#### The Expedition Hall

*The Expedition Hall is packed earth, split posts, blunted steel, blood in the mud, and shouted correction from veterans with no patience for heroic stupidity. New recruits learn quickly that courage is not a defence.*

*A party with an Expedition Hall turns survival into doctrine. The first lesson is how to fall. The second is how to stand before the thing that made you fall reaches you.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** Heroes in your Active Party gain **+1" Speed**.

#### The Undercroft

*The Undercroft is a warren of cellars, sealed drains, hidden doors, and passages older than the Stronghold above it. Smugglers, informants, and quiet killers all find reasons to know its shape.*

*No one admits how deep it goes. Each year another blocked stair is uncovered. Each year the party decides not to ask who carved it.*

**Cost:** See the Component Cost table in **11.3**.

**Benefit:** After deployment, choose 1 Hero in your Active Party. That Hero may **Shift 3"**, then becomes **Hidden** if they are eligible to **Hide**.

### 11.4 Legendary Veterans

A Hero that **Retires** at **Level 10** becomes a **Legendary Veteran** in addition to producing their normal **Retirement Payout**. Record that Legendary Veteran as unassigned. They cannot be assigned during the **Town Phase** in which they are created. Beginning with the party's next **Town Phase**, assign them to one completed Stronghold Component. If no completed Stronghold Component is available, they remain unassigned and may be assigned during a later **Town Phase** after a Stronghold Component is completed.

Each completed Stronghold Component can have only 1 assigned Legendary Veteran. Once assigned, a Legendary Veteran cannot be reassigned.

A **Legendary Veteran** grants the benefit listed for their assigned **Stronghold Component**. This benefit is gained in addition to the **Component**'s normal benefit. Where a Veteran benefit states an improved value with **instead of**, use the improved value in place of the Component's printed value.

| Stronghold Component | Legendary Veteran Benefit |
| --- | --- |
| **The Vault** | **Master of the Treasury:** Your **Vault Reserve** is **40c** instead of **20c**. |
| **The Barracks** | **Drillmaster of the Old Guard:** Once during each **Town Phase**, when a Hero uses **Train [1 TAP]**, reduce that Training Cost by **20c** instead of **10c**. When a Hero uses **Retrain [1 TAP]**, they may replace any number of eligible **Class Talents** and **General Talents** instead of 1. Pay the Retrain cost once. |
| **The Armoury** | **Keeper of Relics:** Choose up to **2 Heroes** instead of 1 when applying the Armoury's benefit. |
| **The Apothecary** | **Physician of Last Resort:** Each Hero in your Active Party may ignore the first Wound they would gain during each adventure. |
| **The Outer Walls** | **Warden of the Threshold:** When your party rolls on a **Journey Table**, roll **4 times** instead of twice and choose 1 result. |
| **The Arcanum** | **Archmage of the Arcanum:** You may use the Arcanum's benefit once per round instead of once per adventure. |
| **The Stronghold Chapel** | **Saint of the Hearth:** Heroes pay no Coin cost when using **Chirurgeon's Care**. |
| **The War Room** | **Marshal of the Campaign:** Your party gains **+4** on Initiative rolls instead of **+2**. |
| **The Expedition Hall** | **Master of Expeditions:** Heroes in your Active Party gain **+2" Speed** instead of **+1" Speed**. |
| **The Undercroft** | **Master of Whispers:** The chosen Hero may **Shift 8"** instead of **3"**. |

### 11.5 Solo and Cooperative Campaign Adjustments

Use this section for **solo** and **cooperative** campaigns.

#### 11.5.1 Campaign Length and Party Structure

A solo or cooperative campaign lasts until the party wins the **Triumph Finale**, loses the **Triumph Finale**, or records **4 permanent Hero deaths**. Record a permanent death when a retained death record is discarded because the Hero was not resurrected before the next adventure. A Hero returned to life before then does not increase this total.

- The allied party fields **1–4 Heroes**.
- **Hirelings** may be recruited and used normally under the core Hireling rules.
- In solo and cooperative campaigns, purchasing Stronghold Components grants the normal benefits, but the campaign does not end early when the fifth Component is purchased.

Eligibility and resolution for the **Triumph Finale** are defined in **11.5.4**. If the party records its fourth permanent Hero death before attempting the Finale, the campaign ends in defeat. If the party loses the Finale, the campaign ends in defeat. Do not resolve **Journey Home**, Aftermath rewards, or a further **Town Phase** after a lost Finale unless the **Triumph Objective** explicitly says otherwise.

#### 11.5.2 Reward and Economy Adjustments

Solo and cooperative campaigns use the outcome grades in **10.5.10** and the reward-banking rules in **10.5.11**.

In addition:

- any reward tied to defeating a Boss is lost if no allied Hero escapes,
- treasure taken from the battlefield must still be extracted to count,
- and any discount or boon granted by a **Journey Table** result applies before normal Town spending begins.

#### 11.5.3 Solo and Cooperative Campaign Generation

Prepare each adventure using **10.5.2 Solo and Cooperative Setup Checklist**. During **Aftermath**, resolve **Journey Home** before entering the **Town Phase**.

If the rolled Core Scenario matches the one used for the immediately preceding adventure, reroll it once and use the new result even if it repeats.

#### 11.5.4 Triumph Finale

In solo and cooperative campaigns, the **Triumph Finale** is the final expedition of the campaign. The party may attempt the Finale once they have completed any **5** different Stronghold Components and the Active Party has **APL 9–10**.

The Triumph Finale uses:

- **1 Triumph Boss**
- **1 Triumph Objective**
- **1 Weather result**
- **1 Awake support Monster Group** generated for the party's starting Party Size

Ignore normal Secondary Objectives during the Triumph Finale unless a specific Triumph Objective says otherwise.

##### Triumph Setup

1. **Battlefield:** Use a standard **36"×36"** battlefield.
2. **Edges:** The party chooses one battlefield edge as the **South** edge. The opposite edge is **North**; the remaining edges are **East** and **West**.
3. **Climate, Terrain, and Weather:** Choose or randomly determine the Finale's Climate and one Core Scenario from that Climate using **10.1.1 Climate and Core Scenario Selection**. Use only that scenario's **Battlefield and Terrain** instructions; ignore its other rules. Then roll **1d6** on that Climate's Weather Table and apply the result.
4. **Boss and Objective:** Roll **1d20** on the Triumph Boss table and **1d10** on the Triumph Objective table. On a Boss result of **16–20**, the party chooses any Boss entry from the table. The Boss forms **Monster Group 1**, begins **Awake**, and has Boss Scale determined under **9.7 The Bestiary**. Place the Boss in the centre or nearest legal space unless the objective's Setup rule changes, splits, or delays Boss placement. Then place the objective's remaining elements as instructed.
5. **Deployment:** All Heroes and active Hirelings deploy within **3"** of the **South** edge.
6. **Support Monsters:** Generate and deploy **1 Awake support Monster Group** as described under **Triumph Support**.
7. **Begin Play:** Begin Round 1 with the **Initiative Phase**. Do not roll **PvE Initiative** for Round 1: the **Party Phase** happens first unless a specific Triumph Objective says otherwise.

##### Triumph Support

Every Triumph Finale generates exactly **1 Awake support Monster Group**. Generate the Group on the Finale Climate's random Monster table for the party's APL band, using the column for the party's starting Party Size. It is **Monster Group 2**. Place it at the midpoint of the North edge, using the nearest legal spaces that are at least **8"** from every allied combatant and **6"** from the Boss where possible. It uses the normal Monster AI rules.

##### Triumph Minions

When a Triumph Objective places one or more **Triumph Minions**, roll once on the row for the Finale Climate to determine the Monster type for that placement event. Place the listed number of that Monster. All Triumph Minions placed by the same Triumph Objective belong to one Monster Group. Assign that Group the next available group number when the objective first places a Triumph Minion. Record that number for the rest of the Finale, and add later Triumph Minions from that objective to the same Group even if none of its earlier Monsters remain. Follow **Monsters Placed After Setup** in **Section 10**. Every Triumph Minion is **Awake**, hostile to the party, and uses their canonical bestiary profile.

If an objective's simultaneous or cumulative Minion limit would be exceeded, place as many Minions as possible without exceeding either limit and ignore the excess.

| Finale Climate | Roll | Triumph Minion |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Greenmark | 1d3 | 1 = Goblin; 2 = Beastman; 3 = Briarling |
| Ashlands | 1d3 | 1 = Undead Warrior; 2 = Ghoul; 3 = Possessed Corpse |
| Undermarches | 1d3 | 1 = Kobold; 2 = Cave Goblin; 3 = Giant Bat |
| Pale City | 1d4 | 1 = Frozen Skeleton; 2 = Snow Goblin; 3 = Ratkin Scavenger; 4 = Frost Ghoul |
| Sun-Drowned | 1d2 | 1 = Fire Beetle; 2 = Skeleton Warrior |
| The Mire | 1d4 | 1 = Bogling; 2 = Swamp Goblin; 3 = Zombie; 4 = Stirge |

##### Triumph Boss Rules

Use the complete **Boss** rules and profiles in **9.7 The Bestiary**, including Boss Scale, control protections, rewards, and **Relentless Assault**. If an objective delays the Boss's placement, the Boss cannot use **Relentless Assault** before being placed.

When selecting a **Primary Target**, a Triumph Boss uses these priorities before their printed priorities:

1. **Objective Pressure:** A legal Hero carrying a required scenario objective, or the legal Hero who most recently resolved a required scenario action this round, while in the Boss's **LOS**. If more than one qualifies, choose the nearest, then the one with the lowest current HP, then use **Random Determination**.
2. **Vengeful Focus:** The last legal Hero to damage the Boss. This priority lasts until another Hero damages the Boss or that Hero is no longer a legal target.
3. The Boss's printed target priorities and normal Monster AI tie-breakers.

##### Triumph Success and Failure

At setup, determine the **Required Extractors**: half the starting Party Size, rounded up, minimum **1**. Unless an objective states a different edge or requirement, every instruction to "extract at least half the party" means the Required Extractors must leave through the **North** edge after the other Victory requirements are complete.

**Victory:** The party wins the Triumph Finale only if it completes the rolled Triumph Objective and satisfies that objective's extraction requirement.

**Defeat:** The party immediately loses if all Heroes are dead, all Heroes are **Knocked Out** with no legal recovery remaining, or the Triumph Objective's fail condition is met. The **Triumph Finale** has no round limit unless the rolled objective explicitly defines one. The Finale ends only when the party achieves the listed **Victory** condition or one of the listed **Defeat** conditions resolves. In a solo or cooperative campaign, losing the **Triumph Finale** ends the campaign in defeat. Do not return to the **Town Phase** after a lost **Triumph Finale**.

At the end of any round, the party may concede the Triumph Finale. Conceding is a **Defeat** and ends the campaign under the same rules.

##### Triumph Objective Table

Roll **1d10**.

Ward-Pillars, Chests, Portal Gates, Beacons, and Altars in this table are scenario objects, not combatants. They cannot take actions or Reactions, gain conditions, or be moved or healed unless their objective says otherwise. If an objective gives an object HP and AV, attacks and damaging effects may target it as though it were visible; it automatically fails any Check it is required to make.

**1. The Arcane Anchors**

**Objective Scaling:** Use the printed Ward-Pillar count for the party's starting Party Size.

**Level Scaling:** Ward-Pillar statistics are fixed. The Boss and support Monsters use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** This objective creates no reinforcements.

**Setup:** Place Ward-Pillars equally spaced around the centre, each at least **8"** from the Boss.

- **1 Hero:** 1 Pillar
- **2 Heroes:** 2 Pillars
- **3 Heroes:** 3 Pillars
- **4 Heroes:** 4 Pillars

Each Pillar has **40 HP** and **AV 2**.

**Special Rules:** The Boss is **Immune** to all damage and conditions while any Pillar remains intact.

**Victory:** Destroy all Pillars, then slay the Boss, then extract at least half the party.
**Failure:** This objective has no round-based failure condition. The party loses only through the defeat conditions in **Triumph Success and Failure**.

**2. The Endless Tide**

**Objective Scaling:** Reinforcement counts and limits use the party's starting Party Size.

**Level Scaling:** The Boss and support Monsters use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** No more than **2 × Party Size** Minions placed by this objective may be on the battlefield at the same time, and this objective can place no more than **3 × Party Size** Minions during the Finale.

**Setup:** Standard.

**Special Rules:** The Boss cannot be reduced below **1 HP** before the end of Round 8. At the start of each Monster Phase, place Triumph Minions equal to the starting Party Size at a randomly determined battlefield edge. Apply this objective's **Reinforcement Limit**.

**Victory:** Survive through the end of Round 8, then extract at least half the party via the North edge by the end of Round 10.
**Failure:** If fewer than the **Required Extractors** remain able to extract, or if the extraction requirement is not met by the end of Round 10, the party loses.

**3. The Artifact Extraction**

**Objective Scaling:** Use the printed Chest count for the party's starting Party Size.

**Level Scaling:** Chest interactions use the printed Check. The Boss and support Monsters use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** This objective creates no reinforcements.

**Setup:** Place sealed Chests along the battlefield midline.

- **1 Hero:** 2 Chests
- **2 Heroes:** 3 Chests
- **3 Heroes:** 4 Chests
- **4 Heroes:** 5 Chests

**Interact [1 AP]:** Open a Chest. Make an **INT Check**.
**Success:** The Chest opens.
**Failure:** The Chest remains closed.

If **2 or more** Chests remain unopened after a Chest is opened, that Chest is empty. When a Chest is opened and exactly **1** Chest remains unopened, roll **1d6**. On **1–5**, the just-opened Chest contains the Artifact. On a **6**, the final unopened Chest contains the Artifact.

A Hero carrying the Artifact drops it in the nearest legal space if reduced to **0 HP**.

**Victory:** Recover the Artifact and extract it via the North edge.
**Failure:** The party loses through the defeat conditions in **Triumph Success and Failure**, or if no Hero can legally reach, carry, or extract the Artifact.

**4. The Gauntlet**

**Objective Scaling:** Use the printed Elite count for the party's starting Party Size. Do not generate the Triumph support Monster Group.

**Level Scaling:** Generate each Elite independently by rolling on the **APL 9–10** band of the Finale Climate's Random Monster Table and using the **4 Heroes** column, regardless of Party Size, until the result contains at least one Elite. Randomly select one Elite from that result. Duplicate results and duplicate Elite names are allowed for this objective. The Boss uses the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** This objective creates no reinforcements after setup.

**Setup:** Do not deploy the Boss at setup. Instead deploy Elite enemies.

- **1 Hero:** 1 Elite
- **2 Heroes:** 2 Elites
- **3 Heroes:** 3 Elites
- **4 Heroes:** 4 Elites

- If 1 Elite is placed, place them at the midpoint of the North edge.
- If 2 Elites are placed, place one at the midpoint of the East edge and one at the midpoint of the West edge.
- If 3 Elites are placed, place one at the midpoint of each of the North, East, and West edges.
- If 4 Elites are placed, use the 3-Elite placement, then place the fourth at one of the two North corners, determined randomly.

All Elites placed by this objective form **Monster Group 1** and begin **Awake**.

**Special Rules:** When the final Elite is slain, immediately deploy the Boss in the centre or nearest legal space. The Hero activation during which the Boss is deployed does not trigger **Relentless Assault**.

**Victory:** Slay the Boss, then extract at least half the party.
**Failure:** The party loses only through the defeat conditions in **Triumph Success and Failure**.

**5. Collapse the Portal**

**Objective Scaling:** Use the printed Portal Gate count for the party's starting Party Size.

**Level Scaling:** Portal Gate statistics are fixed. The Boss and support Monsters use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** No more than **2 × Party Size** Minions placed by this objective may be on the battlefield at the same time, and this objective can place no more than **3 × Party Size** Minions during the Finale.

**Setup:** Place Portal Gates across the centre line.

- **1 Hero:** 1 Gate
- **2 Heroes:** 2 Gates
- **3 Heroes:** 3 Gates
- **4 Heroes:** 4 Gates

Each Gate has **30 HP** and **AV 1**.

**Interact [2 AP]:** Disrupt a Gate. Make a **SPI Check**.
**Success:** Destroy the Gate.
**Failure:** The interaction fails.

**Special Rules:** At the start of each Monster Phase, if any Gate remains intact, place Triumph Minions equal to the starting Party Size within **2"** of a randomly determined intact Gate. Apply this objective's **Reinforcement Limit**. The Boss gains **+2 AV** while any Gate remains intact.

**Victory:** Destroy all Gates, then slay the Boss, then extract at least half the party.
**Failure:** The party loses only through the defeat conditions in **Triumph Success and Failure**.

**6. Banish the Shadows**

**Objective Scaling:** Use the printed Beacon count for the party's starting Party Size.

**Level Scaling:** Beacon interactions use the printed cost. The Boss and support Monsters use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** This objective creates no reinforcements.

**Setup:** Place Beacons in a ring around the centre. The battlefield is in total darkness. Maximum **LOS** is **4"** until all required Beacons are lit.

- **1 Hero:** 1 Beacon
- **2 Heroes:** 2 Beacons
- **3 Heroes:** 3 Beacons
- **4 Heroes:** 4 Beacons

**Interact [1 AP]:** Light an unlit Beacon. The Beacon becomes lit.

**Special Rules:** The Boss cannot be targeted by ranged attacks while fewer than the required number of Beacons are lit.

**Victory:** Light all required Beacons, then slay the Boss, then extract at least half the party.
**Failure:** The party loses only through the defeat conditions in **Triumph Success and Failure**.

**7. The Moving Storm**

**Objective Scaling:** None.

**Level Scaling:** The storm area and damage are fixed. The Boss and support Monsters use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** This objective creates no reinforcements.

**Setup:** Place an **Aura 6"** safe area centred on the battlefield.

**Special Rules:** At the end of each round, the safe area moves **1d6"** using **Random Direction** in **10.1**, stopping its centre at the battlefield edge if necessary. Any allied combatant outside the safe area after it moves suffers **1d10 arcane damage**.

**Victory:** Slay the Boss, then extract at least half the party.
**Failure:** The party loses only through the defeat conditions in **Triumph Success and Failure**.

**8. Purge the Altars**

**Objective Scaling:** Use the printed Altar count for the party's starting Party Size.

**Level Scaling:** Altar statistics are fixed. The Boss and support Monsters use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** This objective creates no reinforcements.

**Setup:** Place Altars near the battlefield centre.

- **1 Hero:** 1 Altar
- **2 Heroes:** 2 Altars
- **3 Heroes:** 3 Altars
- **4 Heroes:** 4 Altars

Each Altar has **35 HP** and **AV 1**.

**Special Rules:** The first time each round the Boss ends an activation within **6"** of an intact Altar, roll **3d8**. The Boss heals HP equal to the result multiplied by Boss Scale.

**Victory:** Destroy all Altars, then slay the Boss, then extract at least half the party.
**Failure:** The party loses only through the defeat conditions in **Triumph Success and Failure**.

**9. The Twin Threat**

**Objective Scaling:** None.

**Level Scaling:** Divide the rolled Boss's final Max HP as printed below. All other Boss values use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** This objective creates no reinforcements.

**Setup:** Split the Boss into Alpha and Omega forms. Both forms belong to **Monster Group 1**, begin **Awake**, and are placed within **6"** of the battlefield centre. Alpha has half the Boss's final Max HP, rounded up. Omega has half, rounded down. Each form otherwise uses the Boss's complete profile. The forms share all Recharge rolls, Recharge states, and limited-use abilities.

**Special Rules:** The forms collectively use the Boss's normal **Relentless Assault** limit. After each triggering Hero activation, only the next form activates. Alternate the scheduled form after every **Relentless Assault** trigger, beginning with Alpha in Round 1; do not reset this sequence between rounds. If the scheduled form is destroyed, the surviving form activates instead, and the Alpha-Omega sequence still advances normally.

At the start of the **Monster Phase**, only the form due to take the next **Relentless Assault** activation (or the surviving form if that form is destroyed) resolves start-of-**Monster Phase** abilities. During the forms' first collective activation each round, only the activating form resolves start-of-activation Special Abilities and **AI Steps**. Later collective activations follow the normal **Relentless Assault** restrictions. If one form is destroyed and the other survives until the end of the round, the destroyed form returns within **2"** of the survivor with **8 × Boss Scale HP**.

**Victory:** Destroy both forms in the same round, then extract at least half the party.
**Failure:** The party loses only through the defeat conditions in **Triumph Success and Failure**. A form destroyed during the same round as the other form's destruction does not revive, regardless of which form was destroyed first that round.

**10. Defend the Innocent**

**Objective Scaling:** Use the printed Civilian count for the party's starting Party Size.

**Level Scaling:** Civilian statistics are fixed. The Boss and support Monsters use the normal Triumph Finale rules.

**Reinforcement Limit:** This objective creates no reinforcements.

**Setup:** Place Civilians in the centre of the battlefield.

- **1 Hero:** 2 Civilians
- **2 Heroes:** 3 Civilians
- **3 Heroes:** 4 Civilians
- **4 Heroes:** 5 Civilians

Each Civilian is an allied scenario combatant with **5 HP**, **AV 0**, **Speed 4"**, and **Sz M**. Civilians have no AP, take no actions or Reactions, automatically fail Checks, do not count as Heroes or Hirelings, and are legal targets for hostile Monsters. Remove a Civilian from play when they are reduced to **0 HP**.

**Special Rules:** While any Hero is a legal target for the Boss, a Civilian is not a legal target for the Boss's non-area attacks or effects. The Boss treats the legal Hero nearest to any surviving Civilian as their highest-priority target. If no Hero is a legal target, the Boss treats the nearest surviving Civilian as their highest-priority target. Civilians do not count when a Boss determines the placement of an Area of Effect. They are still affected if the final area covers them. Other Monsters target and affect Civilians normally. At the end of each Party Phase, move each surviving Civilian up to **4"** toward the South edge. A Civilian that leaves the battlefield through the **South** edge is safely escorted: remove them from the battlefield. A safely escorted Civilian counts as a surviving Civilian.

**Victory:** At least as many Civilians as the starting Party Size survive and the Boss is slain, then extract at least half the party.
**Failure:** If fewer Civilians than the starting Party Size are alive or safely escorted, the party immediately loses.

Roll **1d20**. On a result of **16–20**, the party chooses any listed Triumph Boss.

## Appendix A. Learn to Play

This appendix teaches the first Heraldry Skirmish game using a reduced setup. It does not replace the full rules. It teaches the core loop of initiative, activations, **AP**, movement, attacks, Reactions, Monster AI, carried objectives, and extraction.

A standard competitive game normally uses **4 Heroes per side** on a **36"×36"** battlefield with a full scenario, a **Secondary Objective**, weather, random Monsters, and full party creation. This introductory skirmish instead uses **2 Heroes per side**, **1** neutral Monster Group, **1** carried objective, and **1** **Treasure Chest** on a **24"×24"** battlefield.

In **Grid Mode**, use a **24"×24"** map marked in **1"** squares.

Ignore backgrounds, Hirelings, Summons, weather, Secondary Objectives, campaign rules, and random scenario generation for this first game. Class names identify each Hero's role only. Do not use class talents, ancestry rules, backgrounds, Luck, Powers, or advancement unless they are printed in this section. The full rules in **Sections 2–11** still apply unless this appendix states otherwise.

For this teaching game, do not use the **Injuries Table**. When a Hero is reduced to **0 HP**, they become **Knocked Out**, become **Prone**, drop any carried objective in their current space, and remain **Knocked Out** for the rest of the game.

### A.1 Learn to Play At a Glance

| Element | Learn-to-Play Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Battlefield** | **24"×24"** battlefield. In **Grid Mode**, use a **24"×24"** map marked in **1"** squares. |
| **Sides** | **2 Heroes** per side. |
| **Neutral Monsters** | **4 Dire Wolves**, all **Awake** at the start of the adventure. |
| **Primary Objective** | Pick up and extract the **Dispatch Satchel**. |
| **Secondary Treasure** | Open the **Treasure Chest** for **1c**. |
| **Round Limit** | **4** rounds. |
| **Campaign Rules** | Do not use campaign injuries, advancement, Town actions, backgrounds, Hirelings, Summons, weather, or Secondary Objectives. |

### A.2 What You Need for the First Game

Use the following:

- **1** battlefield measuring **24"×24"**
- **4** Hero miniatures, **2** per side
- **4** Dire Wolf miniatures or suitable stand-ins
- **1** **Dispatch Satchel** marker
- **1** **Treasure Chest** marker
- **4–6** terrain pieces
- Dice, measuring tools, and markers for **AP**, **HP**, and conditions

Place terrain as follows:

- **1** ruined wall or low ruin, about **3"×3"**, at the centre (**Blocking Terrain**)
- **1** low wall, about **2"×3"**, **4–6"** from the centre on one flank (**Impassable Terrain**)
- **1** patch of rubble, about **3"×3"**, **4–6"** from the centre on the opposite flank (**Cover Terrain** tagged **Difficult Terrain**)
- **2–3** additional scatter pieces, each about **2"×3"** or **3"×3"**, around the middle of the battlefield (**Cover Terrain**)

### A.3 Learn-to-Play Parties

Use these fixed Heroes as written. Do not buy equipment, choose backgrounds, or alter these profiles for this teaching game. Edric is the Road Wardens' **Party Leader**, and Varek is the Black Briar Raiders' **Party Leader**.

For this teaching game, ignore equipment requirements, **DEX Pen**, and **Max Speed**. Use only the damage, **AD**, and traits printed here. Choose active Hands equipment before deployment. For this appendix only, changing active Hands equipment costs **0 AP** and may be done immediately before an action or Reaction; the **2 Hands** limit still applies. In the full game, use **Interact [1 AP]** under **7.2**.
