A Monster described as **hostile to all** treats every other combatant as an enemy, including Monsters outside their own Group; Monsters in their own Group remain allied.
- Monsters do not spend AP, use NRG, take **Reactions**, or use ability scores unless a rule explicitly grants them.
- A Monster never makes a Check. An effect that would require one applies automatically unless the Monster is **Immune** to it. A Monster automatically succeeds on every **Terrain Check** (**2.3**).
- Unless a scenario says otherwise, a **Boss** begins **Awake** and uses **Relentless Assault** instead of activating during the **Monster Phase**. Each hostile Hero triggers it once per round after activating. A Hero who spends their last AP on a **Reaction** before activating triggers it after the current activation or effect instead. The Boss cannot exceed the number of starting hostile Heroes. Only their first activation each round resolves start-of-activation Special Abilities and **AI Steps**; every attack step resolves their full printed **Multi-Attack**.
- A Monster has a default perception range of **12"**. A visible enemy for Monster AI must be within perception range and **LOS**. A listed special sense or explicit target range may extend perception as described in **9.5**.
- At the start of a Monster's activation, determine their **Primary Target**, first applying any **Target Priority** printed in a Scenario-Specific Monster's **AI Steps**, then resolve any start-of-activation Special Abilities (**9.6**). Evaluate AI Steps in ascending order; for a step marked **on d6 N+**, roll **1d6** and require **N** or higher. Resolve the first valid AI Step, if any; it ends the activation unless it says the Monster continues. If no AI Step is valid, or the Monster continues, attack an **Engaged** enemy, move toward and attack the **Primary Target**, **Search** for a **Hidden** enemy within **12"** and **LOS**, or return toward the Group's objective or Guard Point.
- The standard **Primary Target** is the nearest visible enemy. Break ties by lowest current HP, then the most recent enemy to damage that Monster, then **Random Determination**.
- When a party-controlled source reduces a **Monster** to **0 HP** or otherwise defeats them, that party collects the Monster's CV. If no party-controlled source defeats the Monster, no party collects that CV unless a rule says otherwise. Competitive play secures collected Monster CV when the adventure ends; solo and cooperative play use the outcome-grade banking rules.
- A named bestiary Monster created by a Monster rule joins the creator's Group, cannot activate until the next Monster Phase, and yields **0 CV** unless a rule says otherwise.

### C.9 Summon Summary

- **Summons** are temporary combatants that their creating rules identify as Summons. A named bestiary Monster placed by a Monster or scenario rule remains a **Monster** unless that rule explicitly identifies them as a Summon.
- An allied **Summon** with no listed AP has **2 AP**. A Summon created during a round gains their full listed or default AP immediately.
- A Summon created by a Power normally takes their activation immediately after the caster's activation. If the Power resolves outside the caster's activation before the caster's side has **Passed**, the Summon activates immediately after the current activation ends, or immediately after the Power resolves if no activation is in progress; if the caster's side has already **Passed**, the Summon does not activate until the next round (**3.3.3**). This is the Summon's only activation that round. Resolve multiple Summons in an order chosen by the caster's controller.
- If a non-Monster **Summon** must make a **STR**, **DEX**, **INT**, or **SPI Check** with a score omitted from their profile, treat that score as **+0** for that Check.

- A Summon's printed attack damage is complete; add no unlisted ability modifier (**2.5.1**).
- Unless a rule explicitly says otherwise, an allied **Summon** cannot take **Reactions**, **Interact**, **Spot**, or **Hide**; carry, claim, control, score, or extract objectives; contribute **Coin Value**; satisfy extraction requirements; or complete campaign objectives.
- A party's limit is **2 allied Summons** in play. If a rule would create a third allied **Summon**, create the Summon, then choose one allied Summon in that party to be dispelled. Resolve the new Summon's "when summoned" effects only if the new Summon remains in play.
- Unless a rule says otherwise, a **Summon** is removed from the battlefield at the end of the adventure.

### C.10 Campaign Summary

A campaign follows this structure:

1. **Expedition Phase**
2. **Skirmish Phase**
3. **Aftermath Phase**
4. **Town Phase**

During the **Aftermath**, record each secured reward in the **Treasury** or **Storage** once; do not record a reward again if it was already added during play. Then resolve casualties and injuries, confirm adventure completion, and roll on the completed expedition's **Journey Table** before the **Town Phase**. During an adventure, an allied Hero adjacent to a death marker may use **Interact [1 AP]** to recover and carry the dead Hero's items to extraction. Journey effects that choose a Hero use only living Heroes from the Active Party that completed the adventure.

Competitive play secures collected Monster CV when the adventure ends unless a scenario says otherwise. In solo and cooperative play, **Major Victory** and **Costly Victory** secure collected Monster CV; **Withdrawal** and **Catastrophe** lose it unless a scenario says otherwise.

During the **Town Phase**, each party normally receives **4 TAP** to spend on Town actions such as trade, healing, magical research, retraining, Stronghold construction, and recruiting persistent support. A party may add no more than **1 new Hero** per Town Phase with **Recruit Hero [1 TAP]**, and its Roster can contain no more than **8 Heroes**. Its Stronghold roster can contain no more than **8 Hirelings**, including Animal Companions. Hirelings are paid party assets and never modify enemy, Boss, reinforcement, or objective scaling. Purchasing a **Stronghold Component** costs **1 TAP**, and a party may purchase no more than **1 Stronghold Component** during the same **Town Phase**.

Starting items gained through **Recruit Hero** cannot be sold, transferred, reassigned, or placed in shared **Storage** until that recruit completes one adventure in the **Active Party**. If the recruit leaves the Roster before then, remove those starting items.

In competitive campaigns, a party that completes any **5** different **Stronghold Components** achieves **Triumph** after the current Town Phase. If both parties do so during the same Town Phase, both achieve Triumph. Solo and cooperative campaigns instead end with the **Triumph Finale** in **11.5.4**, which a party may attempt once it has completed any **5** different Stronghold Components and its Active Party has **APL 9–10**.

#### Pausing and Resuming a Campaign

This is record-keeping guidance only; it does not create a rewind, reset, replay, or save/reload permission. Between adventures, preserve enough of the existing campaign record to resume accurately: the **Roster** and Active Party; each Hero's Level, Wounds, advancement choices, and persistent rewards; **Treasury** and shared **Storage**; Hirelings and Animal Companions; completed Stronghold Components and their benefits; and any death, retirement, Journey result, injury, reward, or other effect that still matters later.

If an adventure itself is paused by agreement, record enough existing battlefield state to continue the same position: round and current phase; activation/Initiative state; current HP, NRG, and AP; conditions and ongoing effects; Monster Group numbers and states; objective and treasure positions/ownership; clocks and scores; delayed reinforcements; and which combatants have already activated. No listed item changes the underlying rules; omit anything that is not relevant to that adventure.

### C.11 Glossary of Terms and Conditions

This is the sole alphabetized glossary for core rules terms, conditions, campaign vocabulary, and reference terminology used throughout the manuscript. The detailed rules in the main sections remain authoritative.

**Acid:** A damage type.

**Active Party:** The Heroes selected from a campaign party's Roster for the current adventure. A standard Active Party contains **4 Heroes**.

**Adamantine:** An item quality. **Adamantine** items are metal for rules that care whether an item is metal. See **7.6**.

**Adjacent:** The horizontal distance and vertical separation between the two spaces or points are each **1"** or less. In **Grid Mode**, the two horizontal positions must overlap or neighbour each other orthogonally or diagonally, and the vertical separation between them must be **1"** or less.

**Advantage:** Add one extra die of the same type to the affected roll, then ignore the lowest single die result among the affected dice. For a d20 **Check**, roll **2d20** and ignore the lower die. If both **Advantage** and **Disadvantage** apply, those rules cancel.

**Aftermath:** Short form of **Aftermath Phase**.

**Aftermath Phase:** The third phase of the campaign cycle, resolved after the Skirmish Phase. Wounds, fates, and rewards are settled here before the **Town Phase**. See **11.2**.

**AI Step:** A numbered Monster AI procedure label such as **AI Step 1** or **AI Step 2**. These labels indicate behaviour priority order only. They are not movement terms and are unrelated to **Shift**. When a step is marked **on d6 N+**, roll **1d6** as that step is evaluated; the step is valid only on **N** or higher.

**Allied:** On your side.

**Ally:** Another combatant on your side. You are not your own ally unless a rule explicitly says otherwise.

**AP:** The resource used to move, attack, cast Powers, interact, and take Reactions.

**APL:** Average Party Level. During an adventure, add the Levels of all Heroes in the **Active Party**, divide by the number of Heroes in that Active Party, then round down. During the following Town Phase, continue using that APL even if Heroes are swapped. Before the first adventure, use the starting Active Party.

**Arcane:** A damage type and magical tradition used by Arcane Spells.

**Area of Effect:** A blast, **Cone**, **Line**, **Aura**, burst, or similar effect that affects an area rather than a single target. In **Tabletop Mode**, a combatant source uses the centre of their footprint as the origin of a non-Aura area unless a rule names another origin point, and a combatant is affected if any part of their rules footprint lies within or touches the area. Areas of Effect cannot penetrate **Blocking Terrain** or a solid floor, roof, or platform. Cover, **Hidden**, and **Invisible** do not protect against an Area of Effect that does not target the combatant directly unless a rule says otherwise. Unless an Area says otherwise, roll its damage once for all affected combatants and use the shared-roll procedure in **2.7.3**.

**Armour Dice (AD):** Dice rolled to generate **AV**. Chest **AD** is rolled automatically against blunt, piercing, and slashing damage; shield **AD** is rolled only through **Block**. Add the result to every applicable source of flat AV. The total reduces only **blunt**, **piercing**, and **slashing** damage.

**Armour Value (AV):** Mitigation against **blunt**, **piercing**, and **slashing** damage, regardless of source. Damage of every other type and HP loss ignore AV. You apply AV automatically whenever you would suffer such damage; it costs no AP and is not a Reaction. AV may be flat or generated by **Armour Dice (AD)**; all AV is treated identically, and a rule that reduces, halves, or ignores AV applies to the total.

**Aura:** An Area of Effect that extends in all directions from its source, centre point, target point, marker, terrain feature, or origin point. In **Grid Mode**, it uses the geometric square-centre rules in **2.7.3**, not the orthogonal and diagonal distance counting in **2.6**. Unless a rule says otherwise, an Aura moves with its source and ends when its source leaves play.

**Awake:** A Monster Group state. **Awake** Monster Groups activate during the **Monster Phase**.

**Base Damage Dice:** The die or dice rolled for an attack before static modifiers and critical bonus dice.

**Beast:** A combatant whose rule gives them the **Beast** tag. Monsters normally gain the tag from the **Beast** Special Ability, and all Animal Companions have it. Beast-targeting rules affect that combatant; the tag has no other effect by itself.

**Bench:** Any Heroes on your Roster not currently in the Active Party.

**Bleeding:** At the end of their activation, a combatant with **Bleeding** loses **2 HP**. This HP loss cannot be reduced by **AV**, **AD**, **Resistance**, or **Immune**. It ends if they regain HP, receive **Bandages**, or a rule removes it. A **Cursed** combatant cannot end **Bleeding** by regaining HP; **Bandages** and condition-removal effects still work.

**Blinded:** You cannot draw **LOS** beyond **2"**. Attack damage rolls and **Checks** that require sight are made with **Disadvantage**.

**Block:** A Reaction used when an attack or effect would deal blunt, piercing, or slashing damage to you while you have a shield equipped. Roll your shield's AD, if any, and add its flat AV to the AV you already apply against that source.

**Blocking Terrain:** Terrain that cannot be entered, moved through, or ended in. It blocks **LOS**.

**Blood Price:** HP loss paid by a Sorcerer when a Sorcery fails its **Casting Check** or when a Sorcery rule requires it. **Blood Price** is HP loss, not damage.

**Blood Surge:** A Sorcery or Sorcerer rule that increases power through blood-fuelled cost or backlash, as defined by the specific rule that grants it.

**Blunt:** A damage type.

**Boss:** A unique LVL 10 Monster used as a capstone threat. Unless a scenario says otherwise, a Boss begins **Awake** and uses **Relentless Assault** instead of activating during the **Monster Phase**.

**Boss Scale:** The multiplier applied to a Boss's printed HP and other listed values. It equals the number of starting Heroes on all sides hostile to the Boss, minimum **1**. Hirelings, Animal Companions, Summons, and other non-Hero allied combatants never contribute. See **9.7 The Bestiary**.

**Burning:** At the end of each round, suffer **1 fire damage**. During your activation, you may spend **1 AP** to end **Burning** on yourself. It also ends if you enter water or a rule removes it.

**Carried Objective:** A scenario marker, treasure item, or protected element carried by a Hero under the default pickup, transfer, drop, and extraction rules in **Section 10**, unless its own scenario rule overrides them.

**Caster Supremacy:** A Caster Automatic Special Ability gained at Level 4. When the Hero casts a damaging **Tier 0** Power, they roll one additional base damage die of that Power's normal base damage die type.

**Casting Check:** The **Check** made to resolve a Power. It uses the casting ability specified by the Power, class, tradition, or item.

**Celestial:** A combatant whose rule gives them the **Celestial** tag. The tag has no effect by itself; rules that affect Celestials say so explicitly.

**Check:** A d20 roll plus the listed ability score or modifier against a target of **12**, unless a rule says otherwise. A non-Monster combatant with no listed value for a required ability score treats that score as **0** for that Check. A Monster never makes a Check; they suffer the failed-Check effect automatically unless they are **Immune** to it, and they automatically succeed on every **Terrain Check**. See **2.3**.

**Climb:** Vertical movement during a **Move** action. Each **1"** climbed costs **2"** of movement and requires a **STR Check** after declaring how far the combatant will climb. On a failure, the combatant does not climb, remains at the starting position, becomes **Prone**, and ends their movement. If that position has no legal support, resolve **Falling** from that point.

**Coin Value:** The wealth a side has secured, measured in coins. It includes banked and secured coins, the **CV** of Monsters that side defeated, the listed value of secured scenario objectives, and the list price of items secured from **Treasure rolls**. A scenario may name a narrower total for its own victory condition.

**Coins:** The game's currency. Written as **Xc**, where **X** is the number of coins.

**Collision:** Forced movement stopped early by **Impassable Terrain**, **Blocking Terrain**, or another combatant. The target stops at the last legal position. Another restriction, a battlefield edge, or missing support beyond a physical edge does not cause a **Collision**. A **Collision** deals no damage by itself; a rule that deals **Collision** damage says so. See **4.4.6**.

**Combatant:** Any Hero, Hireling, Monster, Summon, or other model that can act on the battlefield.

**Contesting Objectives:** A combatant who cannot contest or control objectives cannot use **Interact** on an objective or pick one up, and does not count toward which combatants control, contest, hold, or occupy an objective, zone, or control point. They may keep carrying an objective they already carry. See **Section 10**.

**Cover:** Partial protection. Cover is binary and does not stack. A target that occupies **Cover Terrain** or an area that provides **Cover** has Cover against nonadjacent enemies. A sight line that crosses, or touches the edge or corner of, any terrain feature other than **Open Terrain** outside the two spaces also grants Cover. A sight line crossing another combatant grants Cover only if that combatant is not **Prone** or **Knocked Out** and their **Sz** is the same as or larger than the target's **Sz**. Other rules may grant Cover. Ranged weapon attacks and non-area damaging ranged Powers against a target with **Cover** roll their base damage dice with **Disadvantage**. Harmful **LOS**-based Powers that require a **Check** to affect that target are also made with **Disadvantage**. Cover never applies to melee weapon attacks. Cover granted only by a sight line crossing a combatant does not satisfy any requirement to have Cover in order to become or remain **Hidden**. Areas of Effect and hazards ignore Cover unless a rule says otherwise.

**Cover Terrain:** Terrain that may be entered. It provides **Cover** against nonadjacent enemies. It can be seen into and out of near its edge, but not across its depth.

**Critical Cast:** A natural **20** on a **Casting Check**. The Power succeeds and gains one **Critical Cast** bonus as described in **8.2**.

**Critical Failure:** A natural **1** on a d20 **Check**. Some other rules, such as Parry, may define their own critical failure result.

**Critical Hit:** An attack or damaging Power in which any retained base damage die shows its maximum value. The first listed damage type is its primary damage type and determines its universal **Critical Hit** rider unless a rule says otherwise.

**Critical Success:** A natural **20** on a d20 **Check**. Some attack or reaction rules may also define their own critical success result.

**Cursed:** You cannot regain HP by any means, except through an **Injuries Table** result that returns you to a stated HP value, and cannot end **Bleeding** by regaining HP, including through such a result; **Bandages** and condition-removal effects still work. **Cursed** lasts until the end of the adventure unless a rule removes it, such as **Purify** or a **Potion of Remove Curse**.

**Dangerous Terrain:** Terrain with a listed hazard that applies when a combatant enters it, crosses it, or ends movement or forced movement in it. Unless the terrain rule says otherwise, resolve a given **Dangerous Terrain** feature no more than once per movement or forced movement.

**Darkness:** A visibility state. Every unlit area provides **Cover** against nonadjacent enemies. Darkness does not block or limit **LOS** unless a rule says otherwise.

**Darkvision:** A sense that ignores **Cover** and visual penalties caused solely by nonmagical **Darkness** when determining **LOS** to, targeting, or resolving an effect against a combatant, object, space, or area origin within its listed range. It does not create **Light**, remove **Darkness**, or ignore **Hidden** or **Invisible**. **Magical Darkness** applies normally unless another rule says otherwise.

**Declared State:** A combatant's recorded movement and positional outcome after a legal declaration under **2.6.1 Declared Movement and Positional State**. A **Declared State** remains authoritative until the combatant moves again, is moved by an effect, a battlefield-state change invalidates one of their declared facts, or a rule requires verification.

**Deep Water:** A **Terrain Tag**. Water too deep to stand in. A combatant in **Deep Water** swims at the surface, treats it as **Difficult Terrain**, cannot be **Prone**, and makes attack damage rolls, **STR Checks**, and **DEX Checks** with **Disadvantage**.

**DEX Check:** A **Check** using **DEX**.

**DEX Pen:** The **DEX** penalty listed by a piece of armour or a shield. It applies to the result of the wearer's **DEX Checks**, including **Dodge**, and to any damage total or other value that adds the wearer's **DEX**. Chest armour and shield **DEX Pen** values are added together. See **7.10**.

**Difficult Terrain:** Terrain in which each **1"** moved costs **2"** of movement. In **Grid Mode**, entering a **Difficult Terrain** square costs **2"** of movement for an orthogonal step and **3"** for a diagonal step.

**Disadvantage:** Add one extra die of the same type to the affected roll, then ignore the highest single die result among the affected dice. For a d20 **Check**, roll **2d20** and ignore the higher die. If both **Advantage** and **Disadvantage** apply, those rules cancel.

**Dodge:** A Reaction that uses a **DEX Check**, with a maximum of **+5** from your own DEX score. On success, the triggering source has no effect on you. On failure, resolve the effect normally; on a natural 1, also become **Prone**. See **5.5.2** for sources that cannot be Dodged.

**Elevation:** Height above the battlefield surface. A combatant is at a **higher elevation** than another only when the difference between their elevations is **2"** or more. In **Grid Mode**, each marked elevation level is **1"** and the difference must be at least **2** levels. Attacks against an enemy at a lower elevation roll their base damage dice with **Advantage**. Adjacency and melee distance also use vertical separation under **2.9.9**.

**Empower:** An option on some Powers that modifies the Power's effect when the caster pays an additional **NRG** cost declared at casting. See **Empower** in **Section 8.2**.

**Enemy:** Any combatant not on your side, including opposing party combatants and Monsters, unless a rule says a specific combatant is not an enemy for that interaction.

**Engaged:** Adjacent to at least one enemy that is not **Knocked Out**. A **Knocked Out** combatant is never **Engaged**. See **5.1**.

**Explosion:** An effect that specifically says it explodes. Do not treat every Area of Effect as an **Explosion** unless its rule says so. See **2.7.3**.

**Extract:** To successfully leave the battlefield with treasure, loot, or another carried objective.

**Falling:** The fall origin is the point named by the triggering rule, or the point where the combatant lost support or fell from. Fall distance is the vertical distance between the fall origin and the point where the combatant is placed after the fall. A falling combatant loses **1 HP for every full 1" fallen beyond the first 1"**. After applying this HP loss, they become **Prone** unless a rule says otherwise. Falls of **1"** or less cause no HP loss. This HP loss has no damage type and cannot be reduced by **AV**, **AD**, **Resistance**, or **Immune**. Falling is not movement and does not trigger **Reflex Attack**.

**Fiend:** A combatant whose rule gives them the **Fiend** tag; the **Fiend** Special Ability grants this tag. The tag has no effect by itself; rules that affect Fiends say so explicitly.

**Finesse:** A weapon trait. Attacks made with a **Finesse** weapon add **DEX** instead of **STR** to the damage total. See **7.7**.

**Fire:** A damage type.

**Footprint:** The rules area a combatant occupies. **Sz S** and **Sz M** use a **1"×1"** footprint; **Sz L** uses **2"×2"**; **Sz H** uses **3"×3"**. See **Size and Footprints** in **2.6**.

**Forced Movement:** Movement caused by a rule rather than chosen movement. Forced movement includes **Push**, **Pull**, and **Slide**, and never triggers **Reflex Attack**.

**Frightened:** You cannot willingly move closer to the source while the source is in **LOS**. Attack damage rolls and **Checks** you make against the source are made with **Disadvantage**.

**Guard Point:** The point on the battlefield a Monster Group treats as its anchor for movement, patrol, and response. Usually assigned during scenario setup.

**Heal / Healing:** Restoring lost HP. Healing is reduced or prevented only if a rule says so.

**Heard the Song:** A named condition defined in **9.7 The Bestiary (The Voice Beneath the Bells)**. A Hero with this condition suffers **-1 SPI** until it is removed. Remove it during the **Town Phase** with **Quiet the Bells [1 TAP]** at **The Chapel**.

**Hero:** A player-controlled adventurer and the primary member of a party.

**Hidden:** Prevents attacks, Powers, abilities, and actions that require **LOS** from targeting the combatant, but does not block **LOS**. The first attack, harmful Power, or harmful Special Ability they resolve gains the first applicable benefit in **5.9**, then **Hidden** ends. Their normal **Hide distance** is **2"**; a rule that changes it changes both the requirement for taking **Hide** and the distance at which a nearby enemy ends **Hidden**. **Hidden** also ends under the other triggers in **5.9** and does not prevent Areas of Effect that do not target the combatant directly.

**Hireling:** An allied non-Hero combatant whose profile or granting rule identifies them as a Hireling. A Hireling follows the normal combat rules except where their own rules say otherwise. Hirelings do not count toward Party Size or APL and never modify enemy, Boss, reinforcement, or objective scaling.

**Holy:** A damage type.

**HP:** Hit Points. A profile that lists one HP value uses it as both current and maximum HP unless a rule says otherwise. When a Hero is reduced to **0 HP**, that Hero becomes **Knocked Out** instead of being immediately removed unless a rule says otherwise.

**HP loss:** A reduction of **HP** that is not damage. **AV** and **AD** never reduce **HP loss**, and effects that trigger on damage do not trigger on **HP loss** unless they say so. See **5.4**.

**Huge (H):** A Size category with a **3"×3"** footprint, or **3×3 squares** in Grid Mode.

**Ice:** A damage type.

**Immobilized:** Your Speed becomes **0"**. You cannot **Move**, **Shift**, **Climb**, or **Jump**.

**Immune:** Takes **0 damage** from the stated source or damage type, or ignores the stated condition or effect if a rule says so.

**Impassable Terrain:** Terrain that cannot be entered, moved through, or ended in. It provides **Cover** unless its terrain entry says otherwise. It does not block **LOS**.

**Initiative:** The start-of-round process used to determine Party Phase order and simultaneous timing precedence.

**Initiative Bonus:** A Hero's **INT** + **SPI** (**6.4**). In competitive play, the Party Leader's **Initiative Bonus** is added to their side's Initiative roll (**3.2**). PvE Initiative does not add it (**10.5.4**).

**Initiative Winner:** The side that wins Initiative for the round and chooses which side activates first during the Party Phase.

**Injuries Table:** The d20 table rolled when a Hero is reduced to **0 HP** and survives long enough to resolve the result.

**INT Check:** A **Check** using **INT**.

**Invisible:** Prevents enemies from targeting the combatant with **LOS**-based attacks, Powers, or Special Abilities unless the attacker is adjacent or has a rule that ignores **Invisible**. A melee attack with **Reach** does not by itself allow targeting unless the attacker is adjacent or another rule allows it. An adjacent attacker that cannot ignore **Invisible** rolls the attack's base damage dice with **Disadvantage**. It does not prevent Areas of Effect that do not target them directly. **Invisible** ends after the combatant's first attack, harmful Power, harmful Special Ability, **Push**, or **Trip** resolves unless the effect says otherwise.

**Journey Table:** The d20 table rolled during the **Aftermath Phase** for the completed expedition's Climate. Apply the rolled result immediately. See **11.2.3**.

**Jump:** Horizontal movement during a **Move** action. Each **1"** jumped costs **2"** of movement and requires a **DEX Check** after declaring a legal landing point. A **Jump** cannot increase elevation by more than **1"**. On a failure, the combatant stops at the last legal point before the gap, obstacle, hazard, or landing point, falls **Prone**, and their movement ends; resolve **Falling** only if that point is lower than where the **Jump** began. See **4.4.9**.

**Knocked Out:** You are at **0 HP**. You cannot activate, take actions, voluntarily move, attack, use Powers, use Special Abilities, or take Reactions. You remain **Prone** unless a rule prevents you from being **Prone**. You are never **Engaged**, and you do not make an adjacent enemy **Engaged**. Resolve damage and **HP** loss while **Knocked Out** under **5.8**.

**Large (L):** A Size category with a **2"×2"** footprint, or **2×2 squares** in Grid Mode.

**Legendary Artifact:** A unique named item. A party cannot hold two copies of the same named **Legendary Artifact**; a treasure result that would duplicate one is rerolled once. See **7.6.2** and **7.17**.

**Legendary Veteran:** A Hero that **Retires** at **Level 10** becomes a Legendary Veteran in addition to producing their normal **Retirement Payout**. The Veteran cannot be assigned during the **Town Phase** in which they are created. Beginning with the party's next **Town Phase**, assign the Veteran to one completed Stronghold Component. Once assigned, they cannot be reassigned. A Legendary Veteran grants the benefit listed for their assigned Component. See **11.4**.

**Light Source:** Creates **Light** in its Aura.

**Lightning:** A damage type.

**Line of Sight (LOS):** A legal visual line from a source to a target. Tabletop Mode draws the sight line between the centres of the source and target combatant footprints, markers, terrain features, hazards, or listed points. Grid Mode draws it between the centres of one occupied source square and one occupied target square. If range, **LOS**, and **Cover** apply to the same effect, the same square pair must satisfy all three. If no legal sight line can be drawn, the target is not in **LOS**.

**Lingering Injury:** A persistent negative effect inflicted by results **3–19** on the **Injuries Table** (**5.8.1**). Its ongoing modifiers and restrictions apply while the Hero is not **Knocked Out**. In campaign play, it persists between adventures until removed by **Cleanse Affliction [1 TAP]** during the **Town Phase** (**11.2.4**); in one-off play, it lasts until the end of the adventure. See **5.8**.

**Living Combatant:** Any combatant that does not have the **Undead** or **Construct** ability.

**Luck (Luck Points):** A Hero resource. Spend **1 Luck Point** after seeing an eligible d20 **Check** or damage roll, but before applying consequences. Reroll the entire roll and use the new result. A roll can be rerolled by **Luck** only once. If more than one Hero could spend **Luck**, use the decision order in **2.10**.

**Magical Darkness:** **Darkness** that a rule explicitly describes as magical. Ordinary **Darkvision** does not ignore **Cover** or visual penalties caused by Magical Darkness unless another rule says otherwise.

**Magical Weapon:** A weapon with **Enchanted +X**, a named **Permanent Special Item** weapon, or a weapon a rule explicitly calls magical. **Masterwork, Silvered, Cold Iron, Elven, Sacred, Palesteel,** and **Adamantine** do not make a weapon magical by themselves. A Power, poison, oil, or temporary damage-type change does not make a weapon magical unless the effect explicitly says so.

**Martial Supremacy:** An Automatic Special Ability gained at Level 4. A Martial Hero's weapon attacks roll one additional base damage die. A Hybrid Hero gains that additional die only for weapon attacks made with their **Primary Weapon**. Other applicable sources of additional base damage dice stack normally.

**Max HP:** A combatant's maximum **HP**. A Hero's starting value is Ancestry Base HP plus Class Starting HP Bonus, increased at each Level. **Max HP** cannot fall below **1**. Current **HP** never exceeds **Max HP**. See **6.2**.

**Max NRG:** A caster's maximum **NRG**, equal to Level plus twice their Primary Casting Score, minimum **0**. Martial classes have no **NRG** pool. See **6.4**.

**Max Speed:** The highest **SPD** a combatant may have while wearing a given piece of armour or wielding a given shield. Armour or a shield that lists a **Max Speed** caps **SPD** at that value; if more than one applies, use the lowest. See **7.10** and **7.12**.

**Medium (M):** The default Size category. Medium combatants use a **1"×1"** footprint, or **1×1 square** in Grid Mode.

**Metal Equipment:** Metal Chest armour, shields, weapons, and qualities are defined in **7.2**. Their restrictions on Power and scroll use are defined in **8.2**.

**Monster:** A neutral or hostile non-party combatant controlled by the Monster AI rules.

**Monster Allegiance:** Unless a scenario says otherwise, neutral Monster Groups are allied with one another and hostile to every party. They do not target, become **Engaged** with, or wake because of allied Monsters. A Monster or Group that is **hostile to all** treats every other combatant, including Monsters outside their own Group, as an enemy; Monsters in their own Group remain allied unless a rule says otherwise.

**Monster Group:** A set of **Monsters** that share a group number and activate during the same Group activation in the **Monster Phase**. If no rule sets the order of individual Monsters within the Group, use **Random Determination** as described in **3.4.2**.

**Monster Phase:** The phase in which Monster waking rules are resolved and each **Awake** Monster Group activates.

**Move:** The universal action that lets a combatant move up to their Speed. **Climb** and **Jump** are allowed only during **Move** unless a rule explicitly says otherwise.

**Natural:** A **Terrain Tag**. Roots, undergrowth, foliage, water, mud, sand, snow, ice, or unworked earth or stone. It excludes doors, walls, buildings, stairs, bridges, structural rubble, traps, objectives, Power-created terrain, and scenario hazards unless a rule explicitly labels that feature natural.

**Necrotic:** A damage type.

**Negative Condition:** One of the following conditions: **Bleeding, Blinded, Burning, Cursed, Frightened, Immobilized, Poisoned [dX], Prone, Silenced, Sleeping, Slowed, Stunned,** or **Weakened**. **Hidden, Invisible, Knocked Out,** and **Wounds** are not negative conditions. The term does not include Wounds, scenario-specific states, or lingering injuries unless a rule explicitly says otherwise.

**NRG:** Energy used to cast Powers and activate certain abilities.

**Off-Hand Weapon:** When a Hero equips two one-handed weapons, the equipped weapon not chosen as their **Primary Weapon**. See **6.13**.

**Open Terrain:** Terrain with no effect on movement, **Cover**, or **LOS**.

**Parry:** A Reaction against a melee attack that deals **blunt**, **piercing**, or **slashing** damage. The defender must wield a weapon with the **Parrying** trait or a rule that allows **Parry**, then rolls that weapon's normal base damage dice and normal attack modifier and compares the result to the attack's total damage of every type after **Roll and build damage**, but before mitigation. Success negates all of the attack's damage, not only blunt, piercing, or slashing.

**Party:** One side's allied Heroes and Hirelings. Allied Summons belong to their controlling party for party-wide limits, but are not Heroes, Hirelings, or Roster members.

**Party Leader:** The Hero nominated by a side to anchor that side's Initiative rolls and to make choices assigned to the **Party Leader** by these rules. A party retains that designation for the duration of an adventure even if the **Party Leader** leaves the battlefield or is removed from play. See **6.1** for full rules.

**Party Phase:** The phase in which players activate allied combatants one at a time.

**Party Treasury:** The shared campaign coin total of the party. Only secured or banked Coins are added to it, and each reward is added only once.

**Piercing:** A damage type.

**Poison:** A damage type.

**Poisoned [dX]:** At the end of your next activation, suffer the listed poison damage, then remove **Poisoned**.

**Power:** A supernatural effect that uses the casting rules in **Section 8**.

**Pressure Clock:** A mandatory solo and cooperative pacing rule rolled after scenario setup, unless the scenario assigns a specific Clock. Each clock lists its trigger, escalation, fail threshold, and mitigation. See **10.5.7**.

**Primary Casting Score:** The ability score named on a class entry's **Primary Casting Score** line. It sets **Max NRG** (**6.4**), and the Hybrid Level 7 increase raises it (**6.13**). Martial classes have none. A **Casting Check** uses the ability set by the Power's tradition or entry (**8.2**).

**Primary Target:** The enemy a Monster is currently trying to attack, move toward, or affect. A Scenario-Specific Monster applies any printed **Target Priority** before the normal target priorities. Under standard Monster AI, the **Primary Target** is the nearest visible enemy within the Monster's perception range; ties use lowest current HP, then the most recent enemy to damage that Monster, then **Random Determination**. If the Monster cannot reach any position from which they may attack their **Primary Target** this activation, they retarget under **Blocked Route** in **9.5**.

**Primary Weapon:** A Hero's designated equipped weapon. A two-handed weapon, or the only weapon equipped, is automatically Primary. When a Hero equips two one-handed weapons, choose one as Primary and treat the other as their **Off-Hand Weapon**. See **6.13**.

**Prone:** Melee attacks against you roll their base damage dice with **Advantage**. Ranged weapon attacks made from more than **2"** away roll their base damage dice with **Disadvantage**. You cannot **Block** or **Parry**. Spend **1 AP** to **Stand**. If a **Monster** is **Prone** at the start of their activation, remove **Prone** before resolving their AI.

**Psychic:** A damage type and magical tradition used by Psychic Abilities.

**Psychic Ability:** A Power of the Psychic tradition. See **8.7**.

**Pull X":** Forced movement that moves the target up to **X"** directly toward the source of the effect or toward a specified point.

**Push X":** Forced movement that moves the target up to **X"** directly away from the source of the effect or away from a specified point.

**Random Determination:** The universal fallback when a rule requires 1 random option from a finite set and gives no other procedure. Every eligible option receives an equal chance; use the smallest die that can include all eligible options and reroll excess results. See **2.6.3**.

**Reach:** A weapon, natural attack, or Monster attack trait. A melee attack with **Reach** may target an otherwise valid enemy within **2"** in **Tabletop Mode**, or within **2** squares in **Grid Mode**, including diagonal squares. **Reach** does not change **Engagement**.

**Reaction:** An action declared before the triggering source's damage dice and resolved at its stated timing under **4.5**. Declare result-dependent Reactions in advance too; commit their costs under **4.5**, spending them only if their trigger occurs and they can resolve. Reactions to non-damaging sources use their stated triggers. A combatant may take multiple **Reactions** in the same round, but only one in response to the same action or effect. For each affected combatant, only 1 **Reaction** may be declared by that combatant or on their behalf to modify how the source resolves against them. A **Reaction** used by the source's controller to modify the source's own roll does not count against that limit. A separate action granted by a **Reaction** may trigger **Reactions** normally. An allied **Summon** may spend unspent **AP** on **Reactions** only if a rule explicitly grants that **Summon** **Reactions**; otherwise, that **AP** is discarded at the end of the round.

**Recharge X-Y:** A Monster ability tag. It begins the adventure available; while spent after being used, roll **1d6** at the start of that Monster's activation, and on **X-Y** it becomes available again. A given Recharge ability cannot be used more than once per round unless a rule explicitly says otherwise.

**Reflex Attack:** A Reaction melee attack triggered during an enemy's activation when they leave your melee distance using **Move** or make a ranged attack within it. Normal melee distance is 1" in Tabletop Mode or adjacent in Grid Mode; Reach extends it to 2" or 2 squares. Shift, forced movement, and ranged attacks made as Reactions do not trigger Reflex Attack.

**Relentless Assault:** The Boss activation rule in **9.7 The Bestiary**. Each hostile Hero triggers 1 Boss activation per round after activating. A Hero who spends their last AP on a **Reaction** before activating triggers it after the current activation or effect instead. The Boss cannot exceed the number of starting hostile Heroes. Only the Boss's first activation each round resolves start-of-activation Special Abilities and **AI Steps**. The Boss does not activate during the **Monster Phase**.

**Reload [1 AP]:** A universal action. Ready an equipped weapon with the **Reload** trait so it may attack again. See **4.3.5**.

**Resistance:** The **Resistant** rule. A rule that ignores **Resistance**, or that **Resistance** cannot reduce, ignores **Resistant**. See **5.4.4**.

**Resistant:** Takes half damage, rounded down as normal, from the stated source or damage type.

**Riposte:** Damage dealt to the attacker when a successful **Parry** has a retained base damage die showing its maximum value. A **Riposte** is not an attack.

**Roster:** All Heroes currently belonging to the party in campaign play.

**Round:** The full sequence of **Initiative Phase**, **Party Phase**, **Monster Phase**, and **End of Round**.

**Same-Named Effects:** Two or more ongoing effects with the same name do not stack on the same combatant, item, or area unless a rule explicitly says otherwise; apply only one instance at a time. See **2.1.2 Same-Named Effects**.

**Setup Roll-off:** The Party Leader's controller rolls **1d20** once for their party. The higher result wins, and the winning party makes the listed setup choice. Reroll ties. In solo and cooperative play, the allied party automatically wins and makes the listed winner's choice unless a scenario says otherwise. See **10.1**.

**Shallow Water:** A **Terrain Tag**. Water shallow enough to wade or swim across at the surface. It is also **Difficult Terrain** unless **Swim** or **Amphibious** says otherwise, and it does not grant **Cover** by itself.

**Shift:** A universal action or rule-granted short movement. A combatant may spend **1 AP** to **Shift 1"**. In **Grid Mode**, a diagonal square costs **1"** of **Shift** distance. A **Shift** is not a **Move**, cannot include **Climb** or **Jump**, cannot cross a gap, obstacle, or elevation change that would require **Climb** or **Jump** unless a rule explicitly says otherwise, and does not trigger **Reflex Attack** unless a rule says otherwise.

**Silenced:** You cannot cast Powers, and you cannot use a Special Ability that explicitly requires speech, chanting, or invocation.

**Size (Sz):** A combatant's physical rules category: **Small (S), Medium (M), Large (L),** or **Huge (H)**. Size determines footprint. See **Size and Footprints** in **2.6**.

**Slashing:** A damage type.

**Sleeping:** You immediately fall **Prone** unless prevented. You cannot take actions, voluntarily move, attack, use Powers, use Special Abilities, or take Reactions. Melee attacks against you roll **1** additional base damage die. You remain eligible to activate to end **Sleeping** even with **0 AP**. **Sleeping** ends when you take damage or lose HP, when an adjacent ally uses **Interact [1 AP]** to wake you, or at the end of your next activation. **Sleeping** is not the same as a **Resting** Monster.

**Slippery Terrain:** Terrain that may force a **DEX Check** if a combatant uses voluntary movement to move through it during one activation. On a failure, the combatant becomes **Prone** and their movement ends. If a combatant becomes **Prone** or falls while on **Slippery Terrain**, they slide **2"** in the direction they were travelling or being moved.

**Slowed:** If your Speed is greater than **0"**, halve it, rounded down to a minimum of **1"**.

**Small (S):** A Size category with a **1"×1"** footprint, or **1×1 square** in Grid Mode. A combatant with **Sz S** has **Small**: they cannot equip equipment with the **Heavy** equipment trait and may move through spaces occupied by **Large** or **Huge** combatants during voluntary movement, but cannot end in an occupied space. The Monster Special Ability **Heavy** is unrelated. All other movement rules still apply.

**Sorcery:** A Power of the Sorcery tradition. A **Sorcery** always resolves, but a failed **Casting Check** requires its **Blood Price**. See **8.5**.

**Space:** The area a combatant, marker, hazard, or terrain feature occupies. A combatant's space is their **footprint**, determined by **Sz** under the **Size and Footprints** rules in **2.6**. In **Grid Mode**, it is the square or squares that footprint occupies.

**Speed (SPD):** The distance a combatant may normally move with one **Move**. **SPD** is the abbreviation of **Speed** and is used for all combatants, including **Monsters**.

**SPI Check:** A **Check** using **SPI**.

**Spot:** A universal action. Choose one **Hidden** enemy within **12"** and **LOS**. **Spot** may choose a **Hidden** combatant despite the targeting restriction in **5.9**. Make an **INT Check** or **SPI Check** against **12**, whichever is higher. On success, that enemy loses **Hidden**. **Spot** does not remove **Invisible** unless a rule says otherwise.

**Stand:** The universal action that removes **Prone** from yourself.

**Storage:** The party's shared pool of unequipped items, consumables, and gear between adventures. Coins are tracked separately in the **Party Treasury**.

**STR Check:** A **Check** using **STR**.

**Stronghold:** The party's permanent campaign base. It has **10** available Components, and completing any **5** different Components wins a competitive campaign.

**Stronghold Component:** One of the 10 permanent upgrades a campaign party may build. Components are purchased only during the **Town Phase**. Competitive **Triumph** requires 5 different Components. See **11.3**.

**Stunned:** You cannot take actions, voluntarily move, attack, use Powers, use Special Abilities, or take Reactions. You remain eligible to activate to end **Stunned** even with **0 AP**. **Stunned** ends at the end of your next activation, or immediately if a rule removes it.

**Summon:** A temporary combatant that their creating rule identifies as a Summon. A combatant does not become a Summon merely because a rule places or creates them. In particular, a named bestiary Monster placed by a Monster or scenario rule remains a **Monster** unless that rule explicitly identifies them as a Summon. An allied Summon with no listed AP has **2 AP**, and a Summon created during a round gains their full listed or default AP immediately. Unless a rule says otherwise, a Summon remains in play until they are reduced to **0 HP**, are dispelled through the allied Summon limit, are removed by a rule, or the adventure ends. A party's limit is **2 allied Summons** in play. If an effect would create a third allied Summon for that party, create the Summon, then choose one allied Summon in that party to be dispelled and removed from play. Resolve the new Summon's "when summoned" effects only if the new Summon remains in play. If more than one player controls that party, the player exercising **Party Leader** authority chooses which allied Summon is dispelled. Enemy, neutral, and Monster-created Summons do not count against a party's allied Summon limit unless a rule says otherwise. Unless a rule explicitly says otherwise, an allied Summon cannot take **Reactions**; take the **Interact**, **Spot**, or **Hide** actions; carry, claim, control, or score treasure or scenario objective markers; contribute **Coin Value**; satisfy extraction requirements; or complete campaign objectives. They are removed at the end of the adventure. If an allied Summon is carrying a treasure or scenario objective marker without a rule that allows them, they immediately drop that marker in their current space.

**Sunder:** A Martial Automatic Special Ability gained at Level 7. The Hero's weapon attacks ignore the first **4 AV** of their target. Because all **AV** is treated the same, **Sunder** reduces the target's total **AV**, whether that **AV** is flat or generated by **AD**.

**Swim (X"):** Surface movement across **Shallow Water** and **Deep Water** at the listed Speed. It ignores movement penalties, movement **Checks**, **Difficult Terrain**, and attack, **STR Check**, and **DEX Check** **Disadvantage** caused by water or swimming. Swimming does not change elevation.

**TAP:** Town Action Points spent on Town actions during the Town Phase in campaign play.

**Target:** The combatant, marker, hazard, terrain feature, or point chosen by a rule or action.

**Target Priority:** A Scenario-Specific Monster rule printed before that Monster's numbered **AI Steps**. Apply it when determining the Monster's **Primary Target**. If no listed target is valid, use the normal Monster target priorities. **Target Priority** is not an **AI Step** and does not end the Monster's activation. See **9.5**.

**Temporary HP:** A separate pool of temporary protection that absorbs damage and **HP loss** before normal **HP**. **Temporary HP** is not healing, does not stack with other **Temporary HP** unless a rule says otherwise, is granted as a fixed value without a dice roll, and always expires during step 2 of the **End of Round**. See **5.4.2 Temporary HP**.

**Terrain:** Battlefield features that may affect **LOS**, movement, Cover, hazards, or objectives.

**Terrain Check:** A Check required by the **Climb** or **Jump** rules, by a Terrain Type or **Terrain Tag**, or by a terrain feature or hazard marker that a scenario or Secondary Objective places. A Monster automatically succeeds on every Terrain Check. A Check that a Power, scroll, item, attack, Special Ability, or weather result requires directly is not a Terrain Check. See **2.3**.

**Terrain Tag:** An optional label that adds movement, hazard, or other special rules without changing a terrain feature's Terrain Type. A Terrain Tag does not grant or remove **Cover** by itself. The tags are **Natural**, **Difficult Terrain**, **Dangerous Terrain**, **Slippery Terrain**, **Shallow Water**, and **Deep Water**.

**Terrain Type:** The single exclusive category assigned to each terrain feature, distinct part of a complex feature, or supporting surface at setup. A Terrain Type determines whether the feature may be entered and its default interaction with **Cover** and **LOS**. The types are **Open Terrain**, **Cover Terrain**, **Impassable Terrain**, and **Blocking Terrain**.

**Total Miss:** An attack whose retained base damage dice are all natural **1s**, unless a rule says otherwise. A **Total Miss** deals no damage and ends the attack. See **5.3**.

**Treasure roll:** One roll of **1d100** on the Treasure Table matching the party's current **APL**. Treasure Tables are ordered from least to most valuable. A treasure marker lists the number of Treasure rolls it yields, resolved when that marker is looted. See **7.6.1**.

**Treasury:** A campaign party's shared pool of coins. Coins spent on items, training, Hirelings, and **Stronghold Components** are paid from the **Treasury**. See **11.2**.

**Triumph:** The final campaign victory achieved by completing the Stronghold in competitive play or winning the **Triumph Finale** in solo or cooperative play.

**Vault Reserve:** Temporary spending power granted by the Vault Stronghold Component. It can be spent only during the Town Phase in which it is gained, only on its listed categories, and is lost if unspent. See **11.3**.

**Visible:** A combatant, marker, hazard, terrain feature, or point is visible to you if you have **LOS** to it, it is not **Hidden** from you, and no other rule prevents you from seeing it.

**Vulnerable:** Takes double damage from the stated source or damage type.

**Weakened:** Your attack damage rolls are made with **Disadvantage**.

**Weather Shift:** A Power that temporarily suppresses the adventure's persistent Weather or Cavern Condition. It normally lasts until the end of the current round, but an explicit duration extension applies normally. Only the most recently resolved **Weather Shift** applies; when it ends, the persistent result resumes. A Weather Shift changes only weather effects unless it explicitly says otherwise.

**Wild Shape:** A Druid class feature that transforms the Druid into a listed form, replacing **SPD**, **Sz**, and other listed values. See **6.12**.

**Wound:** A persistent injury marker, separate from a lingering injury. A Hero dies immediately upon suffering a third Wound. See **5.8**.

**Wounded:** A combatant having at least **1 Wound**. Some rules and items have effects that trigger on, or specifically target, Wounded combatants.

### C.12 Play Examples

#### Hero Creation Example

*Elspeth chooses a miniature of a mail-clad pilgrim carrying a mace and lantern. They build the Hero by choosing an ancestry, then a background, then a class, then the starting equipment package that best matches the miniature. Once the profile is complete, they record the Hero's HP, Speed, Size, Luck, ability scores, Special Abilities, and equipped gear before moving on to their next Hero.*

#### Power Casting Example

*Brother Hal spends 2 AP to cast a Divine Prayer with Range 8". The target is in **LOS** and within range, so the Power is declared. Hal rolls 1d20 and adds SPI. Their total is 14, meeting the universal target of 12, so the Power succeeds and its effect is resolved. If Hal had rolled a natural 1, the Power would have critically failed and they would have suffered that tradition's failure effect instead.*

#### Melee Combat Example

*A Raider attacks a Guard with a hand axe. The Guard declares **Parry** before any damage dice are rolled. The Raider then rolls **1d6 = 5**, adds **+2 STR**, and would deal **7 damage**. The Guard rolls a parry total with a shortsword: **1d6 = 5**, plus **+4 STR**, for **9**. The parry succeeds, so the Guard takes **0 damage**. Because the Guard's parry base die was not a maximum result, no **Riposte** damage is dealt back.*

#### Ranged Combat Example

*A Hunter fires a bow at an enemy across the courtyard. A low ruined wall is **Impassable Terrain** and the sight line crosses it, so the target has **Cover**. The bow attack is still legal, but the Hunter rolls the base damage dice with **Disadvantage**. The lower result is used, then DEX is added, and the target resolves their defence normally.*

#### Scenario Generation Example

*Before the battle begins, the players determine the Climate, scenario, weather, and Monster Groups as instructed by the scenario section. They then place terrain, assign each Monster Group a group number and Guard Point, deploy the battlefield, and begin Round 1 with the Initiative Phase.*

#### Monster AI Example

During the **Monster Phase**, Groups 1, 2, and 4 are **Awake**. They activate in ascending group number order: Group 1 first, then Group 2, then Group 4. When Group 2 activates, no rule sets the order of its individual Monsters, so use **Random Determination** to choose which remaining Monster activates next. Each chosen Monster executes the **first valid instruction** of the **Standard Monster AI Script** and ends their activation before another Monster in the Group is chosen. No player chooses to delay or reorder the Groups or their individual Monsters.

#### Hostile AI Step 1 Example

A **Green Dragon** begins their activation with three Heroes clustered in front of them. They roll **5** for **Poison Breath (AI Step 1, on d6 5+)**, so the AI Step is valid. Place the cone using the Monster area-placement priorities, resolve the listed Checks and damage, and end the Dragon's activation.

#### Grid Movement and Multi-Square Example

*A **Large** combatant with a **2×2** footprint takes a **Move** in Grid Mode. After each orthogonal or diagonal step, every square the combatant would occupy must be legal. If one square of the new footprint enters **Difficult Terrain**, use the highest movement cost that applies to any square occupied after that step. The combatant may move through an allied combatant if the normal movement rules allow it, but cannot end the Move overlapping another combatant. This applies **4.4.3** directly; the example creates no additional footprint rule.*

#### Grid LOS and Cover Example

*A Ranger targets a **Large** Monster with a **2×2-square** footprint in Grid Mode. Under **2.6**, test source-square and target-square pairs using one pair for range, **LOS**, and **Cover**. One pair has a sight line that touches the corner of a **Cover Terrain** square but does not pass through that square's interior and crosses no **Blocking Terrain**. That pair has **LOS**, and the touched terrain grants **Cover**. If another legal pair gives the target less Cover, use that pair instead; if Cover is tied, use the shortest range. If every possible pair is blocked by **Blocking Terrain**, a solid floor/roof/platform, or the interior of an intervening **Cover Terrain** square as described in **2.7.2**, the Ranger has no **LOS**.*

#### Monster Route-Resolution Example

*A Monster has a visible **Primary Target** but cannot attack from their current position. Two legal routes lead to the same required attack position: one is **6"** long and one is **7"** long. Under **9.5 F. Movement Priorities**, use the **6"** route because it is the shortest legal route. If two legal routes remain exactly tied after applying every relevant movement priority, determine only that unresolved final choice randomly. Player tactical preference never replaces the printed priorities.*

### C.13 Single-Sheet Rules Summary

Use this double-sided table reference as a summary of common procedures. It does not override the full rules.

#### Size and Footprints Summary

| Sz | Footprint |
| --- | --- |
| **S** | **1"×1" / 1×1 square**; has **Small** |
| **M** | **1"×1" / 1×1 square** |
| **L** | **2"×2" / 2×2 squares** |
| **H** | **3"×3" / 3×3 squares** |

**Small:** Cannot equip equipment with the **Heavy** equipment trait. During voluntary movement, may move through **Large** or **Huge** combatants but cannot end overlapping a combatant. See **2.6**.

#### Side A: Round, Actions, and Combat

##### Adventure Preparation

**1.** APL. **2.** Climate. **3.** Core Scenario. **4.** Secondary Objectives. **5.** Weather. **6.** Setup Roll-off. **7.** Terrain. **8.** Objectives and Markers. **9.** Monsters. **10.** Guard Points. **11.** Party Deployment. **12.** Round 1.

See **10.1** for the complete procedure and **10.1.1** for Climate and Core Scenario selection.

##### Round Sequence

1. **Initiative Phase:** Refresh AP, roll Initiative, resolve start-of-round effects.
2. **Party Phase:** Sides alternate allied activations. Each allied combatant may activate once per round. An activated combatant must spend at least **1 AP** unless they cannot take actions; a **Stunned** or **Sleeping** combatant remains eligible to activate to end the condition even with **0 AP**, taking no actions and spending no AP. Unspent AP may be saved for **Reactions**. A side must **Pass** when it has no eligible combatants left.
3. **Monster Phase:** Resolve Monster waking rules, then activate each **Awake** Monster Group as described in **Section 3.4**.
4. **End of Round:** Resolve end-of-round effects, end effects that last until the end of the round and remove remaining **Temporary HP**, remove unspent AP, then check scoring, extraction, round limits, and victory conditions.

This is the normal order. In solo or cooperative play, **PvE Initiative** may place the **Monster Phase** before the **Party Phase**; resolve each phase once, then proceed to the **End of Round**. That phase order also sets simultaneous-effect priority between allied-side and Monster Group effects; terrain, weather, hazard, and scenario effects remain last.

##### Universal Actions

|Action|Cost|Summary|
|---|---:|---|
|**Move**|1 AP|Move up to Speed.|
|**Shift**|1 AP|**Shift 1"** without triggering **Reflex Attack**.|
|**Attack**|1 AP|Make one melee or ranged attack.|
|**Push**|1 AP|Make a **STR Check** with **Disadvantage**. On a success, **Push** an adjacent combatant **2"**.|
|**Trip**|1 AP|You must be wielding a weapon with **Trip**. Choose a combatant of your **Sz** or smaller within that weapon's **Range** or melee distance. Make a **STR or DEX Check** with **Disadvantage**. On a success, the target becomes **Prone**.|
|**Power**|Varies|Resolve the **Universal Casting Sequence**.|
|**Special Ability**|Varies|Use one activated Special Ability. Every activated Special Ability lists an AP cost, including **0 AP**. Passive and triggered Special Abilities are not actions.|
|**Stand**|1 AP|Remove **Prone** from yourself.|
|**Interact**|1 AP|Interact with an **adjacent** and **visible** battlefield element.|
|**Hide**|1 AP|Become **Hidden** if outside enemy **LOS**, or if you have **Cover** from every enemy with **LOS** and no enemy is within your **Hide distance**. You cannot **Hide** while **Engaged** or while carrying a **Light Source**.|
|**Spot**|1 AP|Make an **INT Check** or **SPI Check** against **12**, whichever is higher, to remove **Hidden** from one eligible enemy.|

A combatant may take the same non-Reaction **0 AP** action only once during each activation unless the action says otherwise. **0 AP Reactions** use their own triggers and frequency limits.

##### Attack Resolution

1. **Declare and verify:** Name the attacker, attack, target, and damage types; confirm melee distance or range, **LOS**, visibility, **Cover**, and target legality.
2. **Declare Reactions:** Resolve redirection and verify legality, then declare all **Reactions**, paying or committing their costs under **4.5**, before any attack damage dice are rolled. **Block**, **Dodge**, and **Parry** resolve in step 4; a ranged-triggered **Reflex Attack** resolves after the attack. Result-dependent Reactions must also be declared now under **4.5**.
3. **Roll and build damage:** Generate the complete damage roll: roll and retain base damage dice with all **Advantage** and **Disadvantage**, resolve permitted changes or rerolls of retained base dice, determine provisional **Total Miss** and **Critical Hit** results, roll all applicable exploding and other damage dice, and add modifiers by type. Before consequences, resolve any **Luck** reroll under **2.10** and rebuild the complete roll from the new result. Using only the final result, resolve any **Total Miss** and end the attack if applicable. Otherwise, resolve **Critical Hit** and other after-roll effects at their stated timings, then state the total for each damage type.
4. **Defend and mitigate:** Resolve the defensive **Reaction** declared in step 2, if any, then apply **5.1.1 Mitigation Order**. No new Reaction may be declared to this attack.
5. **Apply and finish:** Apply the remaining damage, then resolve any remaining **Critical Hit** effects, conditions, **Wounds**, and **Knocked Out** effects.

AV reduces only blunt, piercing, and slashing damage, regardless of source. Damage of every other type and HP loss ignore AV. Keep each damage type separate until mitigation and damage-type modifiers are complete. Apply AV first, then other flat mitigation in an order chosen by the affected combatant's controller. Apply each eligible mitigation value once; if it can reduce more than one damage type, reduce eligible types in the order the source lists them.

For shared damage, declare all **Reactions** and pay or commit their costs under **4.5** before any damage dice are rolled; resolve declaration-triggered effects at their stated timings. Build the shared roll and resolve **Luck**, then resolve each predeclared defence and mitigate separately. No new Reaction may be declared after the roll. See **2.7.3**. Roll non-area multi-target or repeated damage separately unless the effect says otherwise; Powers use the shared-expression default in **8.2**.

##### Combat Reactions

Declare and pay for these **Reactions** before any damage dice of the triggering source are rolled. Resolve **Block**, **Dodge**, and **Parry** during **Defend and mitigate**; a **Dodge** against a source that rolls no damage dice resolves when declared. Resolve **Reflex Attack** at its printed timing. See **4.5** and **5.2**.

|Reaction|Cost|Trigger|Summary|
|---|---:|---|---|
|**Block**|1 AP|An attack or effect would deal blunt, piercing, or slashing damage to you while you have a shield and can take Reactions.|Roll your shield's AD, if any, and add its flat AV to the AV you already apply.|
|**Dodge**|1 AP|An attack or harmful effect from another combatant would affect you.|DEX Check, using a maximum of +5 from your own DEX. Success: the source has no effect on you. Failure: resolve normally. Natural 1: also become **Prone**.|
|**Parry**|1 AP|A melee attack that deals blunt, piercing, or slashing damage targets you while you have a legal parry weapon or rule.|Roll parry weapon damage against the attack's total damage of every type after Roll and build damage, but before mitigation. If all retained base dice are natural 1s, Parry fails, the attack ignores all of your AV, and the attack resolves normally otherwise. Success: suffer none of the attack's damage; effects that do not require the attack to damage you resolve normally.|
|**Reflex Attack**|1 AP|During an enemy's activation, they leave your melee distance using Move or make a ranged attack within it. Shift, forced movement, and ranged attacks made as Reactions do not trigger it.|Make one melee attack with **Disadvantage** on its base damage dice. Declare a ranged trigger before that attack's damage is rolled.|

##### Power Defaults

- A **Critical Cast** grants only one bonus from the first applicable category in **8.2**.
- **Arcane Spells** and **Druidic Rituals** prohibit metal Chest armour, weapons, and shields; **Sorceries** prohibit metal Chest armour. **Divine Prayers** and **Psychic Abilities** are unrestricted. Elven Chest armour and Elven weapons do not count as metal for these restrictions. Apply the same restrictions to scrolls.
- If a Power creates an ongoing effect and gives no duration, it ends at the end of the current round. Named conditions and **Summons** use their own expiry rules.
- During each round, a combatant may benefit from only one **Power or scroll effect** that grants **AP**, refunds **AP**, or reduces an **AP** cost, regardless of when that effect was used.

#### Side B: Conditions, AI, Terrain, and Cover

##### Rules Boundaries

- **Celestial / Fiend:** Explicit creature tags with no inherent effect; the **Fiend** Special Ability grants the **Fiend** tag.
- **Living combatant:** Any combatant without **Undead** or **Construct**.
- **Magical weapon:** **Enchanted +X**, a named **Permanent Special Item** weapon, or explicitly magical; material and craftsmanship qualities alone are insufficient.

##### Conditions

|Condition|Summary|
|---|---|
|**Bleeding**|At the end of their activation, a combatant with **Bleeding** loses **2 HP**. Ends when HP is regained, Bandages succeed, or a rule removes it.|
|**Blinded**|**LOS** maximum **2"**. Sight-based **Checks** and attack damage rolls have **Disadvantage**. Ends at the end of the affected combatant's next activation.|
|**Burning**|Suffer **1 fire damage** at the end of each round. Ends by spending **1 AP**, entering water, or rule removal.|
|**Cursed**|Cannot regain HP by any means except through an **Injuries Table** result. Lasts until the end of the adventure unless removed.|
|**Frightened**|Cannot willingly move closer to the source in **LOS**. Attacks and **Checks** against the source have **Disadvantage**. Ends at the end of the affected combatant's next activation.|
|**Hidden**|Cannot be targeted by attacks, Powers, abilities, or actions that require **LOS**, but does not block **LOS**. The first qualifying harmful effect gains the first applicable **Hidden** benefit, then **Hidden** ends. A rule that changes the distance requirement for Hide changes its detection distance by the same amount. Areas of Effect can still affect them.|
|**Immobilized**|Speed becomes **0"**. Cannot **Move**, **Shift**, **Climb**, or **Jump**. Ends at the end of the affected combatant's next activation.|
|**Invisible**|Cannot be targeted by **LOS**-based effects unless adjacent or ignored by a rule. A melee attack with **Reach** alone does not allow targeting unless the attacker is adjacent or another rule allows it. Areas of Effect can still affect them. Adjacent attacks have **Disadvantage**. Ends after the first attack, harmful Power, harmful Special Ability, **Push**, or **Trip** resolves unless stated otherwise.|
|**Knocked Out**|At **0 HP**. Cannot activate, take actions, voluntarily move, attack, use Powers, use Special Abilities, or take Reactions. Remains **Prone** unless a rule prevents it. Never **Engaged**, and does not make adjacent enemies **Engaged**. Resolve damage and **HP** loss while **Knocked Out** under **5.8**. Ends when HP is restored above **0**.|
|**Poisoned [dX]**|At the end of next activation, suffer listed poison damage, then remove it.|
|**Prone**|Melee attacks against them have **Advantage**. Ranged weapon attacks from more than **2"** have **Disadvantage**. Cannot **Block** or **Parry**. Stand for **1 AP**. A **Monster** removes **Prone** at the start of their activation before resolving AI.|
|**Silenced**|Cannot cast Powers or use vocal Special Abilities. Ends at the end of the affected combatant's next activation.|
|**Sleeping**|Falls **Prone**; cannot act; remains eligible to activate even with **0 AP**. Melee attacks against them roll **1** additional base damage die. Ends on damage, when an adjacent ally spends **1 AP**, or at the end of their next activation.|
|**Slowed**|If Speed is greater than **0"**, it is halved, rounded down to a minimum of **1"**. Ends at the end of the affected combatant's next activation.|
|**Stunned**|Cannot take actions, voluntarily move, attack, use Powers, use Special Abilities, or take Reactions. Remains eligible to activate even with **0 AP**. Ends at the end of their next activation.|
|**Weakened**|Attack damage rolls have **Disadvantage**. Ends at the end of the affected combatant's next activation.|

**Negative conditions:** **Bleeding, Blinded, Burning, Cursed, Frightened, Immobilized, Poisoned [dX], Prone, Silenced, Sleeping, Slowed, Stunned,** and **Weakened** only.

##### Monster AI Flow

1. Determine enemies using the default allegiance rules in **9.3** and any scenario or profile override.
2. Apply any **Target Priority** printed in a Scenario-Specific Monster's **AI Steps** when determining their **Primary Target**.
3. If no printed **Target Priority** produces a valid target, determine the normal **Primary Target**: nearest visible enemy within perception range; ties use lowest current HP, then the most recent enemy to damage that Monster, then **Random Determination**.
4. Evaluate numbered **AI Steps** in ascending order. For a step marked **on d6 N+**, roll **1d6** and require **N** or higher. Resolve the first valid step. Resolving a valid step ends the activation unless that step explicitly says it continues. If no step is valid, or the step continues the activation, proceed to step 5.
5. If **Engaged** with a valid enemy, attack that enemy.
6. Otherwise move toward the **Primary Target** and attack if able. A **Knocked Out** **Primary Target** is attacked once within the Monster's melee distance, even though it does not make the Monster **Engaged**.
7. **Search:** If no enemy is visible but a **Hidden** enemy is within **12"** and **LOS** of the **Monster**, that enemy's controller makes a **DEX Check**. On a failure, that enemy loses **Hidden**. If more than one **Hidden** enemy is within **12"** and **LOS**, apply this to the nearest, resolving ties by **Target Priorities and Tie-Breakers**. The **Monster's** activation then ends.
8. Otherwise move toward the scenario objective, Guard Point, or patrol route.

When a party-controlled source reduces a **Monster** to **0 HP** or otherwise defeats them, that party collects the Monster's CV. If no party-controlled source defeats the Monster, no party collects that CV unless a rule says otherwise. Competitive play secures collected Monster CV when the adventure ends; solo and cooperative play use the outcome-grade banking rules.

##### Terrain and Cover Snapshot

- **Difficult Terrain:** Terrain in which each **1"** moved costs **2"** of movement. In **Grid Mode**, entering a **Difficult Terrain** square costs **2"** of movement for an orthogonal step and **3"** for a diagonal step.
- **Dangerous Terrain:** resolve the listed hazard when a combatant enters, crosses, or ends movement or forced movement in it.
- **Shallow Water:** **Difficult Terrain** that may be crossed by wading or surface swimming. It does not provide **Cover** by itself.
- **Deep Water:** Surface swimming only. It is **Difficult Terrain**; a swimmer cannot be **Prone** and has **Disadvantage** on attack damage rolls, **STR Checks**, and **DEX Checks** unless **Swim** or **Amphibious** says otherwise.
- **Cover:** Partial protection. **Cover** is binary and does not stack. A target that occupies **Cover Terrain** or an area that provides **Cover** has Cover against nonadjacent enemies. A sight line that meets any terrain feature other than **Open Terrain** outside the two spaces also grants Cover. A sight line crossing another combatant grants Cover only if that combatant is not **Prone** or **Knocked Out** and their **Sz** is the same as or larger than the target's **Sz**. Cover granted only by a sight line crossing a combatant does not satisfy any requirement to have Cover in order to become or remain **Hidden**. Ranged weapon attacks and non-area damaging ranged Powers against a target with **Cover** roll their base damage dice with **Disadvantage**. Harmful **LOS**-based Powers that require a **Check** to affect that target are also made with **Disadvantage**. **Cover** never applies to melee weapon attacks. Areas of Effect and hazards ignore **Cover** unless a rule says otherwise.
- **Light Source:** Creates **Light** in its **Aura**. Within that **Aura**, **Darkness** is removed. It does not remove other forms of **Cover**.
- **Darkness:** Every unlit area provides **Cover** against nonadjacent enemies. It does not block or limit **LOS** unless a rule says otherwise. **Magical Darkness** must be explicitly named; ordinary **Darkvision** does not ignore its **Cover** or visual penalties.
- **Natural:** A **Terrain Tag**. Roots, undergrowth, foliage, water, mud, sand, snow, ice, or unworked earth or stone; it excludes structures, structural rubble, traps, objectives, Power-created terrain, and scenario hazards unless explicitly labelled natural.
- **Elevation:** A combatant is at a **higher elevation** than another only when the difference between their elevations is **2"** or more. In **Grid Mode**, each marked elevation level is **1"** and the difference must be at least **2** levels. The higher combatant's attacks against the lower combatant roll base damage dice with **Advantage**. Adjacency and melee distance also use vertical separation under **2.9.9**.

### C.14 Equipment Quick Reference

This summary covers the most common equipment procedures. Use the full item entry when a specific rule differs.

| Procedure | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Equip an item** | Before deployment, meet every listed ability requirement and remain within the location and Hands limits in **7.2**. An item cannot help you meet its own requirement. Use **Interact [1 AP]** to change active Hands equipment under **7.2**; other equipped permanent items remain fixed during the adventure. |
| **Weapon damage modifier** | Add **DEX** with **Finesse**; otherwise add **STR** for melee, the higher of **STR** or **DEX** for **Thrown**, and **DEX** for other ranged weapons. Add the modifier once per attack. |
| **Armour AV** | Automatic and free. Roll equipped Chest **AD** and add applicable flat **AV**, excluding shield AV. |
| **Block [1 AP]** | Add your equipped shield's **AD** and flat **AV** to the **AV** you already apply. |
| **Use a potion** | Spend **1 AP** unless the item says otherwise, then expend it. For a thrown potion, choose an origin point within the listed range and **LOS**, then centre the listed area on that point. A non-thrown potion **Aura** with no listed centre is centred on a point in your space and does not move. Temporary effects normally end at the end of the round. |
| **Apply poison** | Spend **1 AP** to coat one weapon. Resolve an attack's non-poison damage through defence and mitigation first. If any remains, apply its unused eligible flat reductions and damage-type modifiers and combine both final amounts for one HP application; do not repeat mitigation or open another Reaction window. Apply other poison effects afterward and consume the coating. Otherwise it remains until the end of the round. Only one weapon-applied consumable may benefit an attack. See **7.14**. |
| **Read a scroll** | Apply the metal equipment restrictions for the scroll's tradition, spend **1 AP**, make the listed **INT** or **SPI Casting Check** against **12**, resolve success or backlash, then destroy the scroll. Scrolls cost no NRG. If the declared target or initial area would require a higher-**LVL Monster** to make an ability Check, make the scroll's **Casting Check** with **Disadvantage**. |
| **Thrown weapon** | Each individual weapon may make one ranged attack per activation. A **Total Miss** loses that weapon unless its rule says otherwise. Unlost weapons are recovered at the start of the wielder's next activation. |
| **Sell an item** | Gain **50%** of base value, rounded down to the nearest **1c**, unless a rule says otherwise. Starting items gained through **Recruit Hero** cannot be sold until that recruit completes one adventure in the **Active Party**. |
| **Item value** | Use the finished item's printed **Cost (c)** or **Value (c)**. A granted quality with no listed enhanced value leaves the item's existing value unchanged. |

**Metal equipment:** See **7.2** for metal Chest armour, shields, weapons, and qualities. A shield is metal unless its entry says otherwise.

**Material weapon traits:** **Cold Iron** gains its bonus against **Fey**; **Silvered** gains its bonus against **Lycanthropes**; **Sacred** gains its bonus against **Fiends**; **Adamantine** ignores up to **2 AV**. These qualities do not make a weapon magical unless a rule explicitly says otherwise.
